Title: The Swapped Auction Lot
Cast: Dolores Thibault, Walter Merrick, Hollis Okonkwo, Cora Merrick
Plot: Hollis Merrick, an auction house porter, is the only one to notice that the catalogue illustration of a lot is subtly different from the object on the stand. The swap was arranged by Lenore Merrick, the auctioneer, to disguise a forgery as a copy of itself. Hollis writes everything about the swapped auction lot down, in case no one believes it later. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the swapped auction lot, and Hollis starts to suspect Lenore. The case is closed, though the last clue remains in Hollis's pocket.

Title: The Overheard Midnight Call
Cast: Alistair Tregenza, Edmund Pemberton
Plot: Winifred Pemberton, a hotel telephone operator, overhears a call arranging a death at the stroke of midnight and realises it is tonight. The target is Margery Pemberton, the hotel's owner, who has been sleeping in a different room every night of the week. Winifred is forced to make an unpopular choice about the overheard midnight call and faces the consequences alone. The more Winifred learns about the overheard midnight call, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. For one afternoon it seems that the overheard midnight call might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. The last shot is an empty office and a ringing telephone.

Title: The Church-Basement Kitchen
Cast: Winifred Cholmondeley, Neville Haythorne, Edmund Pemberton
Plot: Edmund Bramwell, a union cook in a steel town, organises the wives of striking workers to run a soup kitchen out of a church basement. The mill owner's wife, Winifred Pemberton, quietly donates the supplies, and the workers must decide whether to accept charity from the enemy. Over a long evening, Winifred tells Edmund a story about the church-basement kitchen that nobody else has heard. Late at night, Edmund finds one last clue about the church-basement kitchen that had been overlooked from the start. The last shot is an ordinary morning, with nothing and everything changed.

Title: The Singing Market
Cast: Winifred Pemberton, Neville Haythorne, Winifred Tregenza
Plot: Beatrice Quayle, a market vendor, begins to sing the prices, and the neighbouring stalls join in to form a street opera. Margery Fairweather, the city official, tries to ban the music, only to discover that the harmony is the only thing keeping the fighting stalls apart. For one afternoon it seems that the singing market might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Beatrice writes everything about the singing market down, in case no one believes it later. Over a long evening, Margery tells Beatrice a story about the singing market that nobody else has heard. The curtain falls on thunderous applause and a chorus that will not go home.

Title: The Poisoned Soup
Cast: Dolores Pruitt, Lenore Ostrander, Vernon Thibault
Plot: Marcus Okonkwo, an apprentice chef, is blamed when a dinner party at a manor ends with the host face down in the soup. The poison was in the bowl, not the soup, and Dale Wexcombe, the butler, polished it earlier in the afternoon. Over a long evening, Dale tells Marcus a story about the poisoned soup that nobody else has heard. Nobody agrees on what the poisoned soup really means, least of all Dale. As the season turns, the poisoned soup becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Marcus returns to the quiet village with one question still unanswered.

Title: The Nightly Radio Voice
Cast: Wanda Lindqvist, Dolores Sutterfield, Lenore Thibault, Dolores Thibault
Plot: Marcus Okonkwo, a radio operator on a remote island, speaks every night with a voice from another island who has never given a name. Lenore Ostrander, the voice, is moving, and the last transmission before the move is a set of coordinates and a date. Marcus is forced to make an unpopular choice about the nightly radio voice and faces the consequences alone. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Marcus thinks about the nightly radio voice. Marcus keeps coming back to the nightly radio voice, convinced that the answer is still there. The two begin again in a small house by the sea.

Title: The Window-Cleaner's Witness
Cast: Jodie Mulgrave, Jodie Pemberthy
Plot: Narelle Costain, a high-rise window cleaner, sees through a glass wall the unmistakable moment of a murder on the thirty-first floor. The killer sees Narelle too, and Clive Ironbridge, a lawyer on the floor below, offers a life of luxury in exchange for silence. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Narelle thinks about the window-cleaner's witness. Clive warns that the window-cleaner's witness will ruin everyone involved, and Narelle refuses to listen. The closing shot reveals the true mastermind sitting calmly in the front row.

Title: The Shipped Teapot
Cast: Rohit Vaidya, Aravind Vaidya, Vikrant Bhosekar, Nandini Sengupta
Plot: Sunita, a brave little teapot in a seaside cafe, is accidentally shipped across the ocean in a crate of china. Rohit, a lonely lighthouse, signals the way home, but only once the teapot learns the song of the tide. Sunita writes everything about the shipped teapot down, in case no one believes it later. Nobody agrees on what the shipped teapot really means, least of all Rohit. Sunita is forced to make an unpopular choice about the shipped teapot and faces the consequences alone. Everyone gathers under the stars to celebrate with an enormous, wobbling cake.

Title: The Recycled Water Signal
Cast: Trevor Costain, Shelley Yarrowood
Plot: Gary Costain, a water-reclamation engineer on a desert colony ship, discovers that the recycled water carries traces of a language no crew member speaks. Trevor Pemberthy, the ship's linguist, deciphers the pattern as an invitation to meet whatever has been living in the ballast tanks. For one afternoon it seems that the recycled water signal might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the recycled water signal, and Gary starts to suspect Trevor. Gary writes everything about the recycled water signal down, in case no one believes it later. The survivors set a new course toward a star nobody has named.

Title: The Unseen Reel
Cast: Shinji Hayakeyama, Takeshi Hayakeyama, Sakura Hayakeyama, Yuki Ishizumi
Plot: Shinji Hakamadajima, a ticket collector at an old cinema, finds a reel of film that contains an unseen scene of a famous disappearance. The footage shows Sakura Tachibara, the cinema's founder, walking into the frame and never coming out. Nobody agrees on what the unseen reel really means, least of all Sakura. The more Shinji learns about the unseen reel, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the unseen reel, and Shinji starts to suspect Sakura. In the drawing room, Shinji gathers the suspects and finally explains.

Title: The Walnut-Shell Boat
Cast: Winifred Pemberton, Beatrice Haythorne, Margery Pemberton
Plot: Philippa, a sailing boat made of walnut shell, embarks on a voyage across the kitchen sink. Beatrice, a sponge pirate, offers a map, but the real treasure is the drain at the end of the journey. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Philippa thinks about the walnut-shell boat. Beatrice warns that the walnut-shell boat will ruin everyone involved, and Philippa refuses to listen. The last scene is a long, happy sunrise with everybody still asleep.

Title: The Sack of Flour
Cast: Siu Tsui, Mei Fong, Lan Fong, Wai Tsui
Plot: Yee Yip, a field cook attached to an infantry company, is ordered to carry a single sack of flour through enemy lines. The flour hides a radio part, and Chun Szeto, the lieutenant, is the only person who knows how to assemble it. Nobody agrees on what the sack of flour really means, least of all Chun. The more Yee learns about the sack of flour, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Rumours about the sack of flour spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. A single cross marks the place where the unit made its stand.

Title: The Whispered Call
Cast: Sunita Kolhatkar, Rohit Joglekar, Aravind Joglekar, Devendra Chitnis
Plot: Kabir Chitnis, an emergency-line operator on the night shift, takes a call from a caller who whispers that a house is being watched. The house is Kabir's own, and Aravind Dhawalkar, the caller, is already inside, calmly reading the operator's diary. Aravind warns that the whispered call will ruin everyone involved, and Kabir refuses to listen. Over a long evening, Aravind tells Kabir a story about the whispered call that nobody else has heard. Nobody agrees on what the whispered call really means, least of all Aravind. The conspiracy collapses, and Kabir disappears from public life.

Title: The Last Continental Tree
Cast: Cora Thibault, Eleanor Delacroix, Dale Wexcombe, Cora Hargrove
Plot: Wanda Delacroix, a gardener in a floating city, tends a tree that is the last living thing from a lost continent. Marcus Merrick, the city's governor, wants the tree cut down to fund a new airship dock, and Wanda must decide who will speak for the roots. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the last continental tree, and Wanda starts to suspect Marcus. Over a long evening, Marcus tells Wanda a story about the last continental tree that nobody else has heard. The survivors set a new course toward a star nobody has named.

Title: The Ninth Bell of Varnholt
Cast: Hester Pennywhistle, Lionel Garthwaite, Dorcas Blenkinsop
Plot: The remote Yorkshire village of Varnholt has a church bell that tolls once, unaided, whenever someone in the parish is about to die. The villagers have learned to bar their doors and say nothing. Dr Agnes Fenwick arrives to take over the practice from a predecessor who vanished, and soon counts eight deaths in her first autumn, each preceded by a single clear note in the night. She asks the sexton to let her climb the tower, and he refuses so violently that she suspects he is hiding something. Searching the parish registers, Agnes finds that the number of tolls has been rising by one each decade since the bell was recast in 1791, and that the ninth toll has never been rung. Local legend says it will come for the one who rings the bell, and that is why the bell ropes were cut a century ago. Someone has spliced them together again. Agnes realises that her missing predecessor spent his last weeks measuring the tower and drawing a ninth bell on a sheet of music paper. She follows his notes to the crypt and finds a cast-iron bell with no clapper, hidden behind the altar tomb. The sexton confesses that his family has kept the bell silent for three hundred years by sacrificing a stranger whenever it threatens to ring. He intends to make Agnes the next offering. During a storm that knocks out the village lamps, she climbs the tower with a borrowed rope, and the silent bell begins to sway on its own. Agnes must decide whether to stop the ninth toll or to let it fall on the man who has kept the village afraid. In the final scene the village wakes to a morning without any sound at all.

Title: The Missing Sentence
Cast: Edmund Fairweather, Alistair Bramwell, Beatrice Haythorne, Margery Bramwell
Plot: Margery Tregenza, a court reporter with perfect shorthand, is offered a bribe to leave a single sentence out of a transcript. The sentence names Neville Cholmondeley, the juror who has been asleep for the entire trial, and who is secretly the judge's brother. Neville warns that the missing sentence will ruin everyone involved, and Margery refuses to listen. A week later, the missing sentence has cost Margery a friendship and a good night's sleep. A final meeting on an empty pier settles every account.

Title: The Shipment of Bibles
Cast: Duncan Beaudrin, Duncan Wharnecliffe
Plot: Duncan Gagnard, a retired U.S. marshal, accepts one final assignment to escort a shipment of bibles across hostile territory. The bibles are hollow, and Marguerite Lavoisy, the minister who ordered them, is carrying the town's entire savings to the next county. Nobody agrees on what the shipment of bibles really means, least of all Marguerite. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Duncan thinks about the shipment of bibles. Duncan hangs up the gun belt and stays on the porch.

Title: The Singing Signal
Cast: Wanda Pruitt, Lenore Ostrander, Cora Pruitt
Plot: Vernon Hargrove, a young radio operator on a destroyer, picks up a faint signal of children singing from the middle of the ocean. Dale Hargrove, the captain, orders the crew to ignore it, and Vernon discovers it is a lifeboat full of survivors from the previous convoy. As the season turns, the singing signal becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. The more Vernon learns about the singing signal, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Over a long evening, Dale tells Vernon a story about the singing signal that nobody else has heard. The war ends a week later, and few of the survivors can speak of it.

Title: The Patient's Prophecy
Cast: Murugesan Sivakumaran, Kalyani Natarajan, Pandian Annamalai
Plot: Pandian Chidambaram, a trauma counsellor, is given a patient who recounts, with disturbing precision, a crime that is about to happen. The patient is Kalyani Natarajan, a retired detective, who is trying to warn the counsellor about their own murder. Pandian writes everything about the patient's prophecy down, in case no one believes it later. Pandian keeps coming back to the patient's prophecy, convinced that the answer is still there. As the season turns, the patient's prophecy becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. The conspiracy collapses, and Pandian disappears from public life.

Title: The Submarine Pantry
Cast: Hollis Okonkwo, Walter Sutterfield
Plot: Wanda Okonkwo, a submarine cook, must feed forty men for three weeks with provisions meant for two. Cora Merrick, the engineer, discovers a crate of canned peaches in the torpedo room that nobody remembers loading. The weather turns. A single cross marks the place where the unit made its stand.

Title: The Ten Ponds Map
Cast: Dale Ostrander, Cora Pruitt, Hollis Pruitt
Plot: Eleanor, a young otter apprentice, inherits a leaky rowing boat and a map of ten forgotten ponds. Dale, a tortoise navigator, points out that the tenth pond is the one the apprentice started from. Over a long evening, Dale tells Eleanor a story about the ten ponds map that nobody else has heard. As the season turns, the ten ponds map becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Late at night, Eleanor finds one last clue about the ten ponds map that had been overlooked from the start. The last scene is a long, happy sunrise with everybody still asleep.

Title: The Dim Firefly's Spark
Cast: Wanda Sutterfield, Walter Wexcombe
Plot: Vernon, a young firefly whose light has gone out, joins a travelling night circus in search of a spark. Marcus, the ringmaster, reveals that the light was never missing, only waiting for a really dark night. Vernon is forced to make an unpopular choice about the dim firefly's spark and faces the consequences alone. For one afternoon it seems that the dim firefly's spark might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Vernon writes everything about the dim firefly's spark down, in case no one believes it later. Vernon waves goodbye to the credits and tiptoes home.

Title: Salvage Rights
Cast: Gideon Prattley, Aileen Cavanagh-Rudd, Tobias Mortlake
Plot: Deep-sea salvage diver Rex Maddison is hired by a Sydney insurance syndicate to find a cargo ship that sank off the Great Barrier Reef with a crate of medical supplies. When he reaches the wreck he discovers that the crate is empty and that the hull has been cut open from the inside. His diving partner is attacked the following night, and the syndicate's agent insists the wreck was already plundered years ago. Rex returns to the water with a borrowed camera and photographs the engine room, where he finds a hidden compartment containing a ship's log written in two different hands. The second set of entries describes a mutiny and a secret passenger, and ends with the line that the crew would rather drown than deliver what they were carrying. He realises that the insurance claim is built on a lie, because the ship was scuttled on purpose with the crew still aboard. The syndicate sends two men in a speedboat to destroy the evidence, and Rex has to dive one more time to the wreck with a single tank of air while they cut his anchor line. He hides the log inside a hollow clam shell and surfaces four hundred metres from the boat, floating on his back in the swell. A passing fishing trawler picks him up at dusk. The log is delivered to a maritime tribunal, and the syndicate collapses within the year. The final shot is the empty wreck at dawn, the open hull full of small, curious fish, with the compartment where the log was hidden now brimming with sand.

Title: The Inspectors' Golden Key
Cast: Hollis Okonkwo, Dale Hargrove, Vernon Pruitt
Plot: Walter Sutterfield, a clumsy hotel porter, is mistaken for the mysterious owner of the hotel by a delegation of visiting inspectors.

Title: The Abandoned Bandstand
Cast: Wanda Thibault, Marcus Thibault
Plot: Dale Merrick, a retired cannery foreman in a town that has just lost its only factory, begins repairing the abandoned bandstand on the seafront single-handedly. The council offers to demolish the bandstand for free, and Wanda Delacroix, who once played there, asks Dale to stop before the whole town learns why. Rumours about the abandoned bandstand spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. Late at night, Dale finds one last clue about the abandoned bandstand that had been overlooked from the start. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the abandoned bandstand, and Dale starts to suspect Wanda. The community gathers, and a quiet reconciliation settles over the final scene.

Title: The Bartender's List
Cast: Clive Pemberthy, Bruce Pemberthy
Plot: Bruce Costain, a bartender at a hotel frequented by smugglers, decides to start keeping a list of every secret that is spoken at the bar. Trevor Dunmore, a new regular, asks only to read one line from the list, the line that describes Trevor's own end. Late at night, Bruce finds one last clue about the bartender's list that had been overlooked from the start. Over a long evening, Trevor tells Bruce a story about the bartender's list that nobody else has heard. As the season turns, the bartender's list becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Bruce boards a night train under a new name.

Title: The Altered Transcript
Cast: Lenore Wexcombe, Dale Hargrove, Hollis Wexcombe
Plot: Wanda Hargrove, a court stenographer in a provincial town, realises that the transcript of a famous trial has been altered by someone in the clerk's office. Wanda keeps a private copy in shorthand, and Cora Wexcombe, the judge, offers a promotion in exchange for its destruction. For one afternoon it seems that the altered transcript might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Wanda writes everything about the altered transcript down, in case no one believes it later. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Wanda thinks about the altered transcript. The last shot is an ordinary morning, with nothing and everything changed.

Title: The Water-Stained Poetry Book
Cast: Marcus Hargrove, Marcus Delacroix, Vernon Sutterfield
Plot: Marcus Ostrander, a bookbinder, receives a damaged copy of a poetry collection from a customer who insists on keeping the water stains. The stains hide Dale Delacroix's handwriting, and the poem on the final page is addressed to the bookbinder by name. Marcus is forced to make an unpopular choice about the water-stained poetry book and faces the consequences alone. Marcus keeps coming back to the water-stained poetry book, convinced that the answer is still there. Late at night, Marcus finds one last clue about the water-stained poetry book that had been overlooked from the start. They part tenderly, promising to meet in the spring.

Title: The Climbing Hydroponic Vines
Cast: Hollis Thibault, Hollis Okonkwo, Lenore Lindqvist
Plot: Vernon Pruitt, a botanist on a generation ship, notices that the ship's hydroponic gardens have begun to grow toward a single, unmarked bulkhead. Behind the bulkhead, Dolores Delacroix, the first captain, has been in suspended animation for six centuries and wakes up demanding to know who gave the order to turn. As the season turns, the climbing hydroponic vines becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the climbing hydroponic vines, and Vernon starts to suspect Dolores. Late at night, Vernon finds one last clue about the climbing hydroponic vines that had been overlooked from the start. Vernon transmits the truth to everyone who can still hear it.

Title: The Frozen Case
Cast: Meenal Vaidya, Devendra Sengupta, Sunita Joglekar, Rohit Joglekar
Plot: Aravind Pandharkar, a mountain rescue volunteer, retrieves a climber from a crevasse and finds a locked case frozen to his wrist. The climber wakes and insists that Anjali Kolhatkar, the guide who abandoned him, should be arrested before the case is opened. Rumours about the frozen case spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. Over a long evening, Anjali tells Aravind a story about the frozen case that nobody else has heard. Nobody agrees on what the frozen case really means, least of all Anjali. Aravind survives, though the evidence is never recovered.

Title: The Dead Man's Telegram
Cast: Wai Tsui, Wai Lo, Wai Szeto, Ping Ngai
Plot: Siu Szeto, a telegraph operator at a lonely desert station, receives a message addressed to a man who died last week. More messages arrive from the same sender, each predicting the next day's robbery, and Kwok Kwan, the sheriff, suspects Siu of writing them. Nobody agrees on what the dead man's telegram really means, least of all Kwok. For one afternoon it seems that the dead man's telegram might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. The town has a new law and an old grudge buried deep in the ground.

Title: The Apartment Beehive
Cast: Sakura Aokawa, Daisuke Sakuradaira
Plot: Michiko Mizoguro, an amateur beekeeper in a city apartment, is evicted when forty thousand bees are discovered inside the shared air shaft. The landlord Takeshi Sakuradaira turns out to be violently allergic, and the bees refuse to leave without the neighbour who feeds them. Over a long evening, Takeshi tells Michiko a story about the apartment beehive that nobody else has heard. Nobody agrees on what the apartment beehive really means, least of all Takeshi. Michiko resolves to tell the truth from now on, for roughly a week.

Title: The National Queue Department
Cast: Hollis Lindqvist, Wanda Thibault, Vernon Sutterfield, Dolores Ostrander
Plot: Lenore Hargrove, a bus ticket inspector with a lifelong fear of rules, is promoted to head of a new national department of queues. Eleanor Okonkwo, the minister, secretly wants the department to fail so that the budget can go to a golf course. As the season turns, the national queue department becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Lenore is forced to make an unpopular choice about the national queue department and faces the consequences alone. Lenore resolves to tell the truth from now on, for roughly a week.

Title: The Jar of Teeth
Cast: Cora Thibault, Marcus Okonkwo, Dolores Sutterfield
Plot: Dolores Pruitt, a travelling dentist, arrives in a mining camp to find every miner missing a front tooth and every tooth kept in a jar. The camp boss Lenore Thibault pays for the teeth in gold dust, and Dolores realises the gold has been hidden in the miners' jaws. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the jar of teeth, and Dolores starts to suspect Lenore. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Dolores thinks about the jar of teeth. Dolores rides out at sunrise without looking back.

Title: The Aliens' Questions
Cast: Sunita Dhawalkar, Lata Chitnis, Rohit Kolhatkar
Plot: Rohit Chitnis, a translator for the first human embassy to a distant planet, realises that the aliens speak only in questions. Sunita Joglekar, the ambassador, answers one question wrongly by mistake, and the entire planet falls silent. Rohit writes everything about the aliens' questions down, in case no one believes it later. Over a long evening, Sunita tells Rohit a story about the aliens' questions that nobody else has heard. The survivors set a new course toward a star nobody has named.

Title: The Thirteenth-Floor Passenger
Cast: Wanda Ostrander, Vernon Delacroix, Walter Lindqvist
Plot: Vernon Okonkwo, a night-shift elevator operator in a skyscraper, takes a mysterious passenger to a floor that does not exist. The doors open on Marcus Sutterfield's office, set exactly as it was on the day of an unsolved fire. Late at night, Vernon finds one last clue about the thirteenth-floor passenger that had been overlooked from the start. Vernon keeps coming back to the thirteenth-floor passenger, convinced that the answer is still there. Vernon writes everything about the thirteenth-floor passenger down, in case no one believes it later. Vernon walks home in the rain, a little poorer and a little wiser.

Title: The Numerical Sequence
Cast: Alistair Ashworth, Neville Bramwell, Alistair Fairweather
Plot: Rupert Thackeray, a radio astronomer, intercepts a signal from the local power station that matches a numerical sequence found in an old kidnapping note. The sequence is a key, and Winifred Thackeray, the station director, kidnapped someone long ago who still has not been found. As the season turns, the numerical sequence becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Rupert keeps coming back to the numerical sequence, convinced that the answer is still there. With seconds left, Rupert cuts the one wire that matters.

Title: The Brass Band Strike
Cast: Wilhelmina Pettibone, Orrin Slocumb, Hortensia Gaskell
Plot: In 1949 the town band of Pottsville, Ohio, goes on strike two days before the Fourth of July parade, demanding a raise of fifteen cents per tune and a proper bandstand. The mayor, a vain man who has planned the parade for months, refuses to negotiate and instead recruits the volunteer fire department and a drum corps of Boy Scouts to take their place. The firemen can play only marching songs, and the scouts can play only reveille, so the rehearsal sounds like a parade of alarm clocks. Meanwhile, the striking musicians set up a picket line outside the town hall with a tuba and a hand-lettered banner. The mayor's daughter, secretly engaged to the trombonist, plays peacemaker, and becomes the first woman in the history of the town to conduct. At the parade the scouts march in the wrong direction, the firemen mistake the cue for a fire, and the strikers show up with the tuba in a pickup truck, playing in the opposite lane. The two bands collide at the town square in a joyful cacophony. The crowd cheers wildly, and the mayor, recognising a political opportunity, announces that the band has always deserved its raise. The tuba player is carried off on the shoulders of the fire department. The film ends with the whole town singing out of tune in the square, and the mayor quietly handing the conductor's baton to his daughter, who will keep it for forty years while the band plays on without a single further dispute. Even the striking tuba player, who never intended to settle, admits it was the best parade he ever failed to attend.

Title: The Accidental Sale
Cast: Shinji Hakamadajima, Kimiko Tachibara, Haruto Hakamadajima
Plot: Yuki Tachibara, a stuttering auctioneer, accidentally sells the town hall to a stranger by scratching an itchy nose at the wrong moment. The buyer, Daisuke Tachibara, a polite tourist, refuses to give the building back and moves into the mayor's office. Late at night, Yuki finds one last clue about the accidental sale that had been overlooked from the start. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Yuki thinks about the accidental sale. The film ends with a toast, a collapsed table and a very large cake.

Title: The Empty-House Aria
Cast: Pandian Ayyadurai, Kalyani Chidambaram, Senthil Annamalai, Pandian Thirunavukkarasu
Plot: Lakshmi Ayyadurai, a janitor in a failing opera house, secretly sings the lead role every night after the audience has gone home. Revathi Subramaniam, the retiring diva, has been listening from the balcony for years, and has chosen the janitor as successor. Lakshmi keeps coming back to the empty-house aria, convinced that the answer is still there. A week later, the empty-house aria has cost Lakshmi a friendship and a good night's sleep. The curtain falls on thunderous applause and a chorus that will not go home.

Title: Seven Stones for Hatsue
Cast: Haruhiko Ishizumi, Sayoko Tachibara, Genjiro Aokawa
Plot: In a mountain village famous for its pottery, the aging potter Hatsue has promised to leave her kiln to the apprentice who can fire seven perfectly matched tea bowls before the first snow. Her nephew has the ambition but not the patience, and a quiet orphan girl named Chiyo has the patience but not the courage to compete. Each failed firing teaches both of them something about clay, and about each other. When Hatsue falls ill, the village expects the nephew to sell the kiln to a factory, and Chiyo must decide whether to finish the bowls alone.

Title: The Lonely Jailhouse
Cast: Philippa Tregenza, Beatrice Fairweather, Alistair Tregenza, Winifred Haythorne
Plot: Neville Bramwell, a young deputy with a stammer, is left in charge of a jail with a single prisoner and a gang approaching from the north. The prisoner, Winifred Fairweather, offers to teach Neville to shoot, but only if the deputy teaches the prisoner to read. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the lonely jailhouse, and Neville starts to suspect Winifred. Winifred warns that the lonely jailhouse will ruin everyone involved, and Neville refuses to listen. Neville rides out at sunrise without looking back.

Title: The Inflatable Army
Cast: Karthikeyan Thirunavukkarasu, Lakshmi Natarajan
Plot: Lakshmi Sivakumaran, a decoy balloon operator, inflates a fake army in an empty field every night and removes it before dawn. Kalyani Velusamy, an enemy spy, notes the decoys but reports them as real, in order to protect the field's farmer. As the season turns, the inflatable army becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Lakshmi is forced to make an unpopular choice about the inflatable army and faces the consequences alone. Lakshmi keeps coming back to the inflatable army, convinced that the answer is still there. The war ends a week later, and few of the survivors can speak of it.

Title: Nile Postman
Cast: Samira Fathallah, Hassan El-Sharqawy, Nabila Zakariyya
Plot: Postman Ibrahim Naguib has delivered letters by felucca along a remote stretch of the Nile for thirty years, and the villages treat him as a kind of living newspaper. When the ministry installs a telephone exchange in the nearest town and announces that his route will be abolished, he decides to make one last delivery of every unsent letter he has been carrying in his canvas bag. Among them are a forbidden love letter, an apology from a man to his estranged brother, a bank draft that has expired, and a child's drawing addressed to a father in Cairo who has not written back. Ibrahim sails south for a week, stopping at each village to deliver one letter and to witness the consequences. The apology reconciles two brothers who have not spoken since a land dispute, and the love letter causes a scandal that nearly ends in a duel. At the final village a widow tells him that the father in Cairo died years ago, and asks Ibrahim to read her the drawing aloud. He describes the picture as a child might see it, and the widow smiles. On his return, the villagers have formed a river cooperative to carry mail by boat, and they ask him to be its first chairman. He accepts, with his canvas bag held to his chest, and sails into the evening current. The last image is the empty felucca drifting downstream by itself, its sail catching the late light, carrying nothing but a single unopened envelope.

Title: The Sleeping Child in the Truck
Cast: Eleanor Lindqvist, Hollis Pruitt, Eleanor Delacroix, Eleanor Sutterfield
Plot: Dale Lindqvist, a getaway driver with a conscience, is hired to drive a truck that is supposed to be empty and turns out to contain a single, sleeping child. The child is the only witness to a murder, and Hollis Merrick, the man who hired Dale, wants the driver to deliver her to the wrong address. For one afternoon it seems that the sleeping child in the truck might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. A week later, the sleeping child in the truck has cost Dale a friendship and a good night's sleep. Over a long evening, Hollis tells Dale a story about the sleeping child in the truck that nobody else has heard. The money is never found, and the city quietly changes hands.

Title: The Library of Unwritten Books
Cast: Dale Okonkwo, Eleanor Hargrove
Plot: Cora Wexcombe, a chimney sweep, finds a hidden room in a chimney that contains a library of unwritten books. Walter Thibault, the librarian, is a ghost who needs a story to finish the last shelf and offers to teach the sweep to read. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the library of unwritten books, and Cora starts to suspect Walter. Over a long evening, Walter tells Cora a story about the library of unwritten books that nobody else has heard. As the season turns, the library of unwritten books becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. The final spell is spoken in a whisper, and the world quietly shifts.

Title: The Misdelivered Parcel
Cast: Solange Lavoisy, Hamish Thibodault, Duncan Wharnecliffe, Gilles Sutherby
Plot: Gilles Beaudrin, a courier for a company that delivers parcels across time, accidentally drops a package in the wrong decade. The parcel contains the winning formula for a vaccine, and Odette Wharnecliffe, the recipient in the wrong decade, refuses to give it back. Nobody agrees on what the misdelivered parcel really means, least of all Odette. Over a long evening, Odette tells Gilles a story about the misdelivered parcel that nobody else has heard. Gilles transmits the truth to everyone who can still hear it.

Title: The Wandering Books
Cast: Vernon Wexcombe, Hollis Hargrove
Plot: Marcus, a small hedgehog librarian, discovers that the books in the forest library have begun to rearrange themselves at night. Vernon, a mischievous owl, claims innocence, but the books have learned to follow the owl's voice. Nobody agrees on what the wandering books really means, least of all Vernon. Marcus is forced to make an unpopular choice about the wandering books and faces the consequences alone. For one afternoon it seems that the wandering books might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Everyone gathers under the stars to celebrate with an enormous, wobbling cake.

Title: The Streetcar Briefcase
Cast: Walter Thibault, Hollis Sutterfield
Plot: Wanda Wexcombe, a streetcar conductor, finds a briefcase of cash under a seat and a gun clipped beneath the next.

Title: Kerosene Summer
Cast: Nagabhushanam Pendyala, Sarojini Devarakonda, Ramaswamy Tadepalligudem
Plot: In a drought-struck Andhra village, a bicycle repairman named Raju discovers that the landowner's kerosene tanker has been secretly siphoning water from the village well. He organises the farmers into a night-time convoy of bullock carts to steal the tanker and drive it to the district collector's office. The landowner's hired thugs pursue them across the dry riverbed in jeeps, and the tanker has to be refilled with water at every culvert.

Title: The Lovelorn Knight Tapestry
Cast: Sakura Hayakeyama, Sakura Aokawa, Kimiko Aokawa
Plot: Sakura Mizoguro, a weaver at a tapestry workshop, is asked to reproduce a medieval portrait of a lovelorn knight. The knight looks exactly like Haruto Hakamadajima, the apprentice at the next loom, and the likeness is not a coincidence. The more Sakura learns about the lovelorn knight tapestry, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Sakura keeps coming back to the lovelorn knight tapestry, convinced that the answer is still there. Sakura is forced to make an unpopular choice about the lovelorn knight tapestry and faces the consequences alone. The two begin again in a small house by the sea.

Title: The Wedding Planner's Alibi
Cast: Ligaya Bautistiano, Rodolfo Pasamonte, Perla Aquinaldo
Plot: Cebu wedding planner Marilou Dizon is hired for the most important event of the year, a society wedding that three rival families have each paid her to sabotage. To keep all three clients happy she manufactures a different story for each, and soon cannot remember who believes which version. The florist is blackmailing her, the band thinks she is a detective, and the bride's grandmother has figured out everything and says nothing. On the morning of the wedding, all three families arrive with a plan to expose her.

Title: The Silent Film Heroine
Cast: Sakura Hayakeyama, Yuki Tsugawara, Shinji Sakuradaira, Yuki Tachibara
Plot: Kimiko Aokawa, a mining-town pianist, accompanies a silent film in which the heroine looks eerily like a local widow. Haruto Mizoguro, the widow, rises to speak the film's missing lines, and the audience realises the widow wrote them. Kimiko keeps coming back to the silent film heroine, convinced that the answer is still there. Rumours about the silent film heroine spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. Over a long evening, Haruto tells Kimiko a story about the silent film heroine that nobody else has heard. Kimiko delivers the closing number without a trace of nerves.

Title: The Embroidered Sail
Cast: Hollis Sutterfield, Walter Wexcombe, Dale Pruitt
Plot: Walter Wexcombe, a sailmaker, receives a commission for a sail with an embroidered message that must be read only from the water. Cora Ostrander, the customer, sails away the next morning, and Walter follows in a borrowed dinghy to read the whole text. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the embroidered sail, and Walter starts to suspect Cora. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Walter thinks about the embroidered sail. Walter keeps coming back to the embroidered sail, convinced that the answer is still there. A final kiss closes the season.

Title: The Daily Morse Greeting
Cast: Meenal Joglekar, Nandini Ranadive
Plot: Meenal Bhosekar, a lighthouse keeper on an orbital beacon, receives a daily greeting in Morse from a station that was decommissioned decades ago. The sender, Kabir Joglekar, is a maintenance bot that has been waiting for a reply so long that it has begun to compose poetry. The more Meenal learns about the daily Morse greeting, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Meenal thinks about the daily Morse greeting. Late at night, Meenal finds one last clue about the daily Morse greeting that had been overlooked from the start. Meenal transmits the truth to everyone who can still hear it.

Title: The Handcuffed Briefcase
Cast: Vernon Merrick, Eleanor Pruitt, Dale Thibault
Plot: Marcus Hargrove, a ticket inspector on an overnight train, finds a briefcase handcuffed to a seat with no passenger in sight. Hollis Delacroix, the passenger who owns it, has been sitting in the dining car all along, patiently waiting for someone else to blink. Marcus writes everything about the handcuffed briefcase down, in case no one believes it later. Hollis warns that the handcuffed briefcase will ruin everyone involved, and Marcus refuses to listen. The money is never found, and the city quietly changes hands.

Title: The Silent Grand Piano
Cast: Eun-ji Jo, Ji-ho Yoon, Ji-ho Baek, So-ra Seo
Plot: So-ra Kwon, a former child prodigy now repairing pianos in a small shop, is asked to tune an instrument that has not been played since a famous disaster. Inside the piano, So-ra finds a folded score that proves Hye-jin Han, a celebrated composer, never wrote the work that made a fortune. The more So-ra learns about the silent grand piano, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Over a long evening, Hye-jin tells So-ra a story about the silent grand piano that nobody else has heard. So-ra is forced to make an unpopular choice about the silent grand piano and faces the consequences alone. In the end, So-ra accepts what cannot be repaired and begins again at dawn.

Title: The Blinking Star Photograph
Cast: Eleanor Merrick, Hollis Delacroix, Wanda Pruitt
Plot: Cora Lindqvist, a night-sky photographer, captures a photograph of a star that is blinking in a pattern spelling the names of everyone in a small town. Dale Wexcombe, an old astronomer, recognises the pattern as an inventory, and recalls an ancient promise to return for the names on the list. For one afternoon it seems that the blinking star photograph might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the blinking star photograph, and Cora starts to suspect Dale. Dale warns that the blinking star photograph will ruin everyone involved, and Cora refuses to listen. The survivors set a new course toward a star nobody has named.

Title: The Forged Prescription
Cast: Walter Wexcombe, Lenore Pruitt, Walter Hargrove, Hollis Merrick
Plot: Hollis Lindqvist, a pharmacist, fills a prescription for a man whose signature matches that of a colleague who died in an accident. Dolores Delacroix, the dead colleague's twin, appears at the counter asking for the same drug, a trigger for a poison no one else knows about. Nobody agrees on what the forged prescription really means, least of all Dolores. Dolores warns that the forged prescription will ruin everyone involved, and Hollis refuses to listen. The conspiracy collapses, and Hollis disappears from public life.

Title: The Child-Shaped Robot
Cast: Dmitri Tomashevsky, Pavel Kuznetsov, Svetlana Rostovtsev
Plot: Natalya Zaitsev, a robot repair technician in a flooded city, receives a damaged companion bot that insists it is a human child. Pavel Dobrolyubov, the bot's former owner, reveals that the machine was built from the recordings of a real child who disappeared. For one afternoon it seems that the child-shaped robot might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Nobody agrees on what the child-shaped robot really means, least of all Pavel. The machine is switched off, but its last question remains unanswered.

Title: The Children Who Follow the Van
Cast: Zeynep Tunçdemir, Burak Yaşarel, Cem Özdilek, Emre Aksoylu
Plot: Selin Gökbulut, an ice cream van driver in a small town, notices a line of children who follow the van and never seem to get older. Burak Polatkan, the oldest of them, politely asks to be given a lift to a field where the van has been parked for sixty years. Late at night, Selin finds one last clue about the children who follow the van that had been overlooked from the start. As the season turns, the children who follow the van becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Over a long evening, Burak tells Selin a story about the children who follow the van that nobody else has heard. Selin survives until dawn, but something is still watching from the window.

Title: The 6:40 Bus
Cast: Shelley Dunmore, Clive Mulgrave, Narelle Pemberthy, Trevor Tolhurst
Plot: Jodie Ironbridge, a bus driver on a route that is about to be cancelled, decides to keep the 6:40 service running with only one regular passenger. The passenger, Clive Pemberthy, finally confesses that the daily trip is the only way to avoid being at home when the bailiffs arrive. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the 6:40 bus, and Jodie starts to suspect Clive. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Jodie thinks about the 6:40 bus. Jodie is forced to make an unpopular choice about the 6:40 bus and faces the consequences alone. The last shot is an ordinary morning, with nothing and everything changed.

Title: The Twenty-Minute Tremors
Cast: So-ra Bae, So-ra Oh
Plot: Dong-hyun Baek, a seismologist on a tidally locked planet, records tremors that arrive on a precise twenty-minute schedule. Tae-yang Oh, the colony's founder, confesses that the tremors are a countdown and that the planet's other half is not uninhabited. The more Dong-hyun learns about the twenty-minute tremors, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Dong-hyun thinks about the twenty-minute tremors. Dong-hyun is forced to make an unpopular choice about the twenty-minute tremors and faces the consequences alone. Dong-hyun transmits the truth to everyone who can still hear it.

Title: The Apartment Photographs
Cast: Vernon Okonkwo, Marcus Wexcombe, Hollis Merrick, Wanda Okonkwo
Plot: Vernon Thibault, a typist in a lawyer's office, finds that the lawyer's confidential files include a set of photographs of the typist's own apartment. Hollis Lindqvist, the lawyer, explains that the pictures were taken to protect the typist, and that the real watcher is across the street. Rumours about the apartment photographs spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. As the season turns, the apartment photographs becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Vernon writes everything about the apartment photographs down, in case no one believes it later. Hollis pays for the mistakes, and Vernon pays for the rest.

Title: The Misspelled Orders
Cast: Hamish Sutherby, Gilles Sutherby, Solange Sutherby, Solange Beaudrin
Plot: Duncan Wharnecliffe, a typist at army headquarters, notices that every copied order contains one misspelled word. The misspellings, when read together, are the plan of an attack, and Odette Chapdelaine, the general's aide, is deliberately sending them to the other side. Over a long evening, Odette tells Duncan a story about the misspelled orders that nobody else has heard. Odette warns that the misspelled orders will ruin everyone involved, and Duncan refuses to listen. A single cross marks the place where the unit made its stand.

Title: The Cigarette Tray Messages
Cast: Haruto Tsugawara, Kimiko Hakamadajima
Plot: Haruto Sakuradaira, a nightclub cigarette girl, discovers that a rival gang is using the tray to pass messages. Daisuke Sakuradaira, the club owner, learns the code and tells the girl to keep delivering, and to start inventing new messages. The more Haruto learns about the cigarette tray messages, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. For one afternoon it seems that the cigarette tray messages might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Daisuke pays for the mistakes, and Haruto pays for the rest.

Title: The Anonymous Flowers
Cast: Revathi Chidambaram, Revathi Annamalai, Senthil Velusamy, Lakshmi Ayyadurai
Plot: Karthikeyan Natarajan, a bicycle courier, delivers a flower to a stranger every morning on behalf of a sender who insists on staying anonymous. The sender is Pandian Ayyadurai, whose own deliveries have become the quietest romance in the city. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Karthikeyan thinks about the anonymous flowers. Karthikeyan writes everything about the anonymous flowers down, in case no one believes it later. The two begin again in a small house by the sea.

Title: Salt Lantern
Cast: Imogen Quayle, Edmund Ashworth, Philippa Hollis
Plot: After her husband drowns in a storm, lighthouse keeper's widow Morwenna Tregarth refuses to leave the rock where she has lived for thirty years. The harbour authority plans to automate the light and send an engineer to remove her. Over a bitter winter, the young engineer and the stubborn widow begin an uneasy friendship, trading stories of the sea and of the people it has taken. When a fishing boat is lost in a blizzard, the two must keep the old lamp burning by hand through a long night.

Title: The Commuter's Melody
Cast: Zeynep Polatkan, Cem Tunçdemir, Emre Yaşarel, Selin Özdilek
Plot: Aylin Gökbulut, a ferry musician, plays the same melody each evening for a commuter who never applauds and never looks up. Zeynep Gökbulut, the commuter, is deaf, and has been counting the rhythm on the rail with a fingertip. Rumours about the commuter's melody spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. Late at night, Aylin finds one last clue about the commuter's melody that had been overlooked from the start. The two begin again in a small house by the sea.

Title: The Seasonal Honey
Cast: Wanda Lindqvist, Eleanor Thibault, Wanda Merrick
Plot: Dale Pruitt, a young beekeeper, discovers that the hive makes honey that tastes of different seasons depending on who eats it. Walter Wexcombe, a king, requests a jar to taste a summer that was missed, and the honey gives the king what has not been earned. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Dale thinks about the seasonal honey. The more Dale learns about the seasonal honey, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Late at night, Dale finds one last clue about the seasonal honey that had been overlooked from the start. The final spell is spoken in a whisper, and the world quietly shifts.

Title: The Matching Inscription
Cast: Cora Delacroix, Wanda Sutterfield, Dolores Ostrander, Hollis Ostrander
Plot: Dale Merrick, a gravedigger with an eye for handwriting, notices that the inscription on a new headstone matches a threatening letter sent to the parish. The mason Wanda Ostrander cut both, on the orders of a parishioner who intended the headstone to be a warning. As the season turns, the matching inscription becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the matching inscription, and Dale starts to suspect Wanda. Dale writes everything about the matching inscription down, in case no one believes it later. The culprit is led away, and the guests depart in uneasy silence.

Title: The Empty Hotel Room
Cast: Winifred Pemberton, Gethin Haythorne
Plot: Alistair Ashworth, a disgraced newspaper photographer, is paid to take pictures of an empty hotel room and discovers someone moved the furniture. Gethin Fairweather, the client, wants the photographs to prove the room was never occupied, and has a gun to prove the point. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Alistair thinks about the empty hotel room. The more Alistair learns about the empty hotel room, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. For one afternoon it seems that the empty hotel room might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Gethin pays for the mistakes, and Alistair pays for the rest.

Title: The Lost Tuba
Cast: Marcus Hargrove, Walter Delacroix, Hollis Hargrove, Marcus Okonkwo
Plot: Lenore Okonkwo, a teenage tuba player in a marching band, loses the instrument two hours before the national parade. Wanda Pruitt, a pawnbroker, lends a monstrous antique horn, and the band discovers that it only plays one harmony. Over a long evening, Wanda tells Lenore a story about the lost tuba that nobody else has heard. Rumours about the lost tuba spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. The curtain falls on thunderous applause and a chorus that will not go home.

Title: The Weight of Feathers
Cast: Percival Dunthorne, Marigold Oakenshott, Jocasta Wrenfield
Plot: An ornithologist on the Shetland island of Unst is found dead in a birdwatching hide with a heron's feather clutched in his hand. Retired postmistress Edie Lumsden, who has delivered letters to every house on the island for forty years, is the only person who notices that the feather comes from a bird that does not live north of Yorkshire. She starts asking where a stranger could have found it, and discovers that three households received parcels from the same mainland address in the week of the murder.

Title: The Wrong Peal
Cast: Walter Merrick, Walter Okonkwo, Hollis Delacroix, Cora Thibault
Plot: Marcus Wexcombe, a young bellringer, notices that the church peal rung at a funeral does not match the order printed in the service. The peal is a code written by Dolores Lindqvist, the vicar, who wants the congregation to find the coffin's real occupant. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Marcus thinks about the wrong peal. A week later, the wrong peal has cost Marcus a friendship and a good night's sleep. As the season turns, the wrong peal becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. The case is closed, though the last clue remains in Marcus's pocket.

Title: The Empty Warehouse Fire
Cast: Alistair Fairweather, Margery Ashworth, Beatrice Lockhart
Plot: Imogen Ashworth, an insurance claims adjuster, is asked to evaluate a fire that destroyed an entire warehouse and nothing inside it. Edmund Fairweather, the owner, produces a lavish inventory of lost goods, none of which has ever been manufactured. Imogen is forced to make an unpopular choice about the empty warehouse fire and faces the consequences alone. Imogen writes everything about the empty warehouse fire down, in case no one believes it later. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Imogen thinks about the empty warehouse fire. Imogen boards a night train under a new name.

Title: The Bakery on Quill Street
Cast: Mireille Lavoisy, Duncan Sutherby, Odette Wharnecliffe
Plot: When the owner of a failing Montreal bakery dies, his two feuding children must run the shop together for ninety days to inherit it. Gilles, a pompous chef, and Odette, a cynical accountant, cannot agree on a single loaf. A viral photograph of a collapsed cake, however, makes the bakery famous overnight, and customers begin queueing around the block for the worst pastries in the city. The siblings decide to lean into the disaster.

Title: The Self-Walking Boots
Cast: Lenore Pruitt, Eleanor Sutterfield, Dolores Thibault
Plot: Eleanor Delacroix, a travelling cobbler, mends a pair of boots that can walk themselves home from anywhere.

Title: The Pre-Embalmed Body
Cast: Dale Wexcombe, Hollis Pruitt, Eleanor Okonkwo, Vernon Thibault
Plot: Dolores Hargrove, a coroner's assistant, notices that the body on the table was embalmed before the time of death in the report. Eleanor Pruitt, the coroner, signed both documents under duress, and slides a key across the desk. Dolores writes everything about the pre-embalmed body down, in case no one believes it later. Eleanor warns that the pre-embalmed body will ruin everyone involved, and Dolores refuses to listen. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the pre-embalmed body, and Dolores starts to suspect Eleanor. The last shot is an empty office and a ringing telephone.

Title: Paper Boats in the Monsoon
Cast: Aravind Joglekar, Anjali Moitra, Devendra Chitnis
Plot: In Kolkata during the monsoon, a young translator named Tara receives a stack of unsigned love letters written in Bengali and accidentally delivered to her door. Determined to find the intended reader, she follows the clues through bookshops and tea stalls, and meets Rohan, a quiet printer who recognises the handwriting. As the rains intensify and the letters run out, Tara realises that the writer has been describing her all along.

Title: Teacher of the Third Valley
Cast: Lin Shuqing, Gao Zhenguo, Meng Xiaoyun
Plot: A young teacher from Shanghai is assigned to a school in the mountains of Yunnan where the only textbook is a worn atlas and half the students walk four hours each way. Teacher Wei Lan begins by trying to follow the curriculum and ends by throwing it away, teaching arithmetic through the prices of tea and geography through the footsteps of the mule drivers. When the provincial inspector announces that the school will be closed for low attendance, the villagers walk all night to carry every child to the examination hall.

Title: The Cartographer's Daughter
Cast: Beatrix Vandenhuyl, Rufus Cartwell-Pike, Eulalia Marchetti
Plot: When explorer Josiah Quill dies in a Panama hotel, he leaves his daughter Maren half a map and a brass sextant that points in the wrong direction. Maren, a trained surveyor who has never left Boston, inherits the expedition's debts and an invitation from a rival explorer to complete the journey together. She suspects that the rival wants the second half of the map for himself, so she leaves him behind and sails for the Orinoco with a one-legged riverboat captain and a stowaway botanist. The river is mapped wrongly on purpose: Quill drew every bend a little off so that nobody could follow him. Maren works out the pattern by comparing the sextant readings to the stars, and learns to read her father's errors as a hidden cipher. Deep in the interior, the party finds a flooded mission whose bell tower rises from the water like a lighthouse, and inside it a chest of survey notes proving that the lost city her father sought was a hoax invented to attract investors. The rival catches up with a company of armed men, still determined to sell the legend. Maren trades the chest for safe passage upriver, then destroys the maps page by page so that no one else will be deceived. She returns home with an accurate chart of the river, the first anyone has drawn honestly, and uses it to open her own surveying firm. The film closes on Maren pinning the new chart above her desk, with a small tear in one corner where her father once rested his thumb.

Title: The Canal Gates
Cast: Imogen Tregenza, Alistair Quayle, Neville Haythorne, Gethin Pemberton
Plot: Neville Thackeray, an elderly lock-keeper on a canal that no longer carries cargo, receives an official notice to stop opening the gates. Neville ignores the order, and Rupert Bramwell, a young surveyor sent to enforce it, falls in love with the rhythm of the water. A week later, the canal gates has cost Neville a friendship and a good night's sleep. Late at night, Neville finds one last clue about the canal gates that had been overlooked from the start. Nobody agrees on what the canal gates really means, least of all Rupert. Neville leaves the old life behind, lighter and finally free.

Title: The Doomed Bridge
Cast: Bruce Dunmore, Clive Yarrowood
Plot: Bruce Mulgrave, a bridge engineer behind enemy lines, is ordered to build a crossing that will be destroyed the next day. Clive Ironbridge, the enemy colonel, admires the work, and asks for the plans to build a copy in peacetime. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the doomed bridge, and Bruce starts to suspect Clive. Nobody agrees on what the doomed bridge really means, least of all Clive. Bruce returns home to a town that has already moved on.

Title: The Diner Photograph
Cast: Yuki Hakamadajima, Michiko Tachibara
Plot: Michiko Tachibara, a snowbound trucker, takes shelter in a roadside diner where the only other customers are sitting in the exact positions of a photograph on the wall. Yuki Hakamadajima, the waitress, has been in the photograph for fifty years, and slides a menu across the counter that lists only Michiko's name. Yuki warns that the diner photograph will ruin everyone involved, and Michiko refuses to listen. Late at night, Michiko finds one last clue about the diner photograph that had been overlooked from the start. Michiko keeps coming back to the diner photograph, convinced that the answer is still there. The last frame reveals that the danger has simply moved on to the next door.

Title: The 3:03 Transaction
Cast: Nandini Vaidya, Rohit Bhosekar
Plot: Kabir Sengupta, a bank's night auditor, finds a single transaction in the books that moves money to a dead account every night at 3:03. The dead account belongs to Rohit Dhawalkar, who is alive, and who has been using it to buy an alibi. A week later, the 3:03 transaction has cost Kabir a friendship and a good night's sleep. Kabir writes everything about the 3:03 transaction down, in case no one believes it later. For one afternoon it seems that the 3:03 transaction might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Kabir survives, though the evidence is never recovered.

Title: The Cassette Tapes
Cast: Margery Ashworth, Rupert Pemberton, Imogen Cholmondeley, Neville Bramwell
Plot: Neville Bramwell, a widowed shepherd, takes in an unsociable teenage boy who arrives with a suitcase of unlabelled cassette tapes. The tapes are recordings of Beatrice Fairweather, the boy's mother, narrating a lifetime of lies, and the boy wants Neville to help him decide whether to play them. Beatrice warns that the cassette tapes will ruin everyone involved, and Neville refuses to listen. The more Neville learns about the cassette tapes, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. In the end, Neville accepts what cannot be repaired and begins again at dawn.

Title: The Lone Whistle's Song
Cast: Walter Sutterfield, Vernon Wexcombe, Dale Delacroix, Lenore Wexcombe
Plot: Dolores, a tin whistle at the bottom of a toy chest, hears the first note of a song from a distant room. Marcus, a drum, joins in from a different box, and the entire toy chest forms a band. Rumours about the lone whistle's song spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. Dolores keeps coming back to the lone whistle's song, convinced that the answer is still there. Everyone gathers under the stars to celebrate with an enormous, wobbling cake.

Title: The Blank Postcard
Cast: Wai Ngai, Lan Kwan, Yee Tsui
Plot: Chun Ngai, a postman on a remote island, delivers a postcard with no stamp and a blank back from a town that no one has visited. Mei Kwan, the island's sole resident, reads the invisible ink under a lamp and weeps. Late at night, Chun finds one last clue about the blank postcard that had been overlooked from the start. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the blank postcard, and Chun starts to suspect Mei. Chun returns to the quiet village with one question still unanswered.

Title: The Empty Island Charts
Cast: Min-jun Seo, So-ra Bae, Hye-jin Han, Hye-jin Kwon
Plot: Seo-yeon Oh, a seaplane pilot, picks up a passenger who pays double and asks to be dropped on an island that is shown as empty on every chart. On the island, Eun-ji Baek is waiting with a rifle, and explains politely that the passenger was bait. Seo-yeon keeps coming back to the empty island charts, convinced that the answer is still there. The more Seo-yeon learns about the empty island charts, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Seo-yeon is forced to make an unpopular choice about the empty island charts and faces the consequences alone. Seo-yeon survives, though the evidence is never recovered.

Title: The Undelivered Letters
Cast: Wanda Okonkwo, Walter Wexcombe, Hollis Pruitt
Plot: Walter Merrick, a translator of love letters for immigrant families, falls in love with the author of the letters that never arrive. Eleanor Pruitt, the author, has been writing them for the translator all along, in a language Walter cannot yet read. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the undelivered letters, and Walter starts to suspect Eleanor. Late at night, Walter finds one last clue about the undelivered letters that had been overlooked from the start. They part tenderly, promising to meet in the spring.

Title: Orbit of the Last Orchard
Cast: Natalya Sokolova, Pavel Orlov, Irina Lebedeva
Plot: On a failing space station the last botanist, Yelena Marchenko, tends a small orchard of apple trees that the crew regards as a harmless eccentricity. When the station's reactor starts to fail and command orders the evacuation of all biological samples, Yelena discovers that the trees have been quietly cleaning the station's air for years. She hides in the orchard and bargains with the crew: if the trees go, so does their only chance of surviving the journey home.

Title: The Deckhand Band
Cast: Kemal Aksoylu, Aylin Polatkan, Zeynep Yaşarel, Zeynep Tunçdemir
Plot: Selin Aksoylu, a ship's cook with a wooden spoon and a remarkable tenor, forms a band of deckhands during a long crossing. Aylin Polatkan, the captain, forbids music on board, but the crossing is saved when the band's rhythm steadies the ship during a mutiny. Selin writes everything about the deckhand band down, in case no one believes it later. Rumours about the deckhand band spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. The festival becomes an annual tradition, with everyone in the key of their choice.

Title: Pashmina
Cast: Simranjit Gulzarpal, Kuldeep Brarwal, Amarpreet Sandhawalia
Plot: A Kashmiri shawl weaver named Noor sells her best pashmina every spring at a fair in Amritsar, where a young Punjabi truck driver, Gurmeet, buys the same shawl every year without ever unfolding it. When Noor finally asks why, he admits that he is sending them to his mother in Canada, who has been losing her sight and wants to feel the weave. Noor begins to include a short verse in each shawl, stitched into the hem where only fingers can find it. By the fourth spring the verses have become a conversation.

Title: The Winning Stub
Cast: Lenore Sutterfield, Marcus Hargrove, Cora Wexcombe, Wanda Merrick
Plot: Dolores Sutterfield, a mother of four working two jobs, finds a stranger's wallet containing a winning lottery stub that expires at midnight. The wallet belongs to Lenore Hargrove, who is sleeping in a doorway three streets away and cannot be persuaded to take the money. For one afternoon it seems that the winning stub might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Dolores thinks about the winning stub. Lenore warns that the winning stub will ruin everyone involved, and Dolores refuses to listen. The last shot is an ordinary morning, with nothing and everything changed.

Title: The Self-Playing Key
Cast: Eleanor Ostrander, Vernon Merrick, Dale Ostrander, Dale Delacroix
Plot: Cora Merrick, a retired piano tuner, is asked to find out why a grand piano in a country house plays one key by itself every midnight. The key is wired to a hidden mechanism in the cellar, and Hollis Hargrove, the estate's lawyer, has been using it to signal an accomplice. Cora writes everything about the self-playing key down, in case no one believes it later. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the self-playing key, and Cora starts to suspect Hollis. The culprit is led away, and the guests depart in uneasy silence.

Title: The Midnight Patient
Cast: Edmund Bramwell, Imogen Quayle, Margery Cholmondeley, Winifred Fairweather
Plot: Beatrice Haythorne, a village doctor, gets a late-night visit from a man with a gunshot wound who refuses to say how it happened. Winifred Bramwell, a policeman, arrives looking for the same man, and the doctor must decide which of them is lying. Beatrice keeps coming back to the midnight patient, convinced that the answer is still there. Beatrice writes everything about the midnight patient down, in case no one believes it later. The more Beatrice learns about the midnight patient, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Beatrice survives, though the evidence is never recovered.

Title: The Unsold Seat
Cast: Walter Okonkwo, Vernon Pruitt, Eleanor Sutterfield
Plot: Marcus Okonkwo, a quiet airline mechanic, discovers that a flight that has just landed has an extra seat that was never sold. Wanda Ostrander, the passenger who occupied it, is nowhere on the manifest, and has left a package marked for the next flight. Over a long evening, Wanda tells Marcus a story about the unsold seat that nobody else has heard. Late at night, Marcus finds one last clue about the unsold seat that had been overlooked from the start. Marcus survives, though the evidence is never recovered.

Title: The Blizzard Birth
Cast: Revathi Velusamy, Vasanthi Annamalai, Kalyani Chidambaram, Lakshmi Velusamy
Plot: Murugesan Thirunavukkarasu, a prairie midwife, rides through a blizzard to deliver a baby in a homestead whose family feuds with the next valley over. The rival family arrives at dawn, led by Pandian Thirunavukkarasu, to ask the midwife to sit with their own dying elder. The more Murugesan learns about the blizzard birth, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Murugesan keeps coming back to the blizzard birth, convinced that the answer is still there. Murugesan hangs up the gun belt and stays on the porch.

Title: The Anonymous Violin Pupil
Cast: Sunita Vaidya, Devendra Dhawalkar
Plot: Sunita Vaidya, a young violin teacher, accepts a pupil who plays beautifully but refuses to say who taught the instrument. Rohit Ranadive, the pupil, is the child of a famous soloist who vanished, and the tune being played is the soloist's last composition. For one afternoon it seems that the anonymous violin pupil might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Sunita is forced to make an unpopular choice about the anonymous violin pupil and faces the consequences alone. Sunita delivers the closing number without a trace of nerves.

Title: The Lost-Luggage Cage
Cast: Pandian Velusamy, Karthikeyan Subramaniam
Plot: Lakshmi Subramaniam, a ferry ticket seller, realises that a gang is using the lost-luggage cage to move stolen jewellery between two countries. Pandian Thirunavukkarasu, the harbour master, has quietly looked away for years, and offers Lakshmi a share to keep looking at the water. Lakshmi keeps coming back to the lost-luggage cage, convinced that the answer is still there. Over a long evening, Pandian tells Lakshmi a story about the lost-luggage cage that nobody else has heard. Lakshmi writes everything about the lost-luggage cage down, in case no one believes it later. The money is never found, and the city quietly changes hands.

Title: The Staircase Shell
Cast: Mei Fong, Lan Chow, Siu Yip, Kwok Ngai
Plot: Kwok, a young snail with a spiral shell shaped like a staircase, sets out to climb the tallest garden wall. Chun, a patient robin, offers a lift, but the snail wants to reach the top by climbing every step. Nobody agrees on what the staircase shell really means, least of all Chun. Kwok writes everything about the staircase shell down, in case no one believes it later. Kwok finally reaches the end of the journey and giggles.

Title: The Railroad Survey Stakes
Cast: Wanda Wexcombe, Marcus Sutterfield, Eleanor Ostrander
Plot: Walter Lindqvist, a young Pawnee tracker, is hired by a railroad survey party to find the safest route through sacred ground. Dale Pruitt, the surveyor, secretly moves the stakes each night, and Walter learns the new line crosses the old burial hills. Over a long evening, Dale tells Walter a story about the railroad survey stakes that nobody else has heard. As the season turns, the railroad survey stakes becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. The town has a new law and an old grudge buried deep in the ground.

Title: The Song-Eating Hatchling
Cast: Edmund Bramwell, Beatrice Cholmondeley, Alistair Thackeray, Gethin Lockhart
Plot: Edmund Haythorne, an apprentice dragon-keeper, is left in charge of a hatchling that eats only songs. Rupert Bramwell, the village choirmaster, discovers that the dragon has swallowed the choir's best hymn and refuses to sing it back. Edmund keeps coming back to the song-eating hatchling, convinced that the answer is still there. The more Edmund learns about the song-eating hatchling, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Nobody agrees on what the song-eating hatchling really means, least of all Rupert. Edmund takes up the burden gladly and sets out at first light.

Title: The Extra Voice on the Tape
Cast: Gary Pemberthy, Jodie Tolhurst, Gary Tolhurst
Plot: Bruce Dunmore, a sound engineer restoring an old radio drama, hears a voice on the master tape that was never part of the script. The voice begins to answer Bruce's questions through the studio speakers, and Trevor Yarrowood, the original actor, was reported dead on the day of the recording. Over a long evening, Trevor tells Bruce a story about the extra voice on the tape that nobody else has heard. Trevor warns that the extra voice on the tape will ruin everyone involved, and Bruce refuses to listen. Only a recording of the final hour remains, and nobody dares to play it.

Title: The Blank Crystal Ball
Cast: Dolores Pruitt, Wanda Wexcombe
Plot: Dolores Ostrander, a carnival fortune teller who has never believed in the act, receives a visitor whose future cannot be seen. The visitor is Eleanor Delacroix, who has no reflection and wants to know the date of Dolores's death, politely, so that the invitation can be sent. Eleanor warns that the blank crystal ball will ruin everyone involved, and Dolores refuses to listen. Dolores is forced to make an unpopular choice about the blank crystal ball and faces the consequences alone. Dolores writes everything about the blank crystal ball down, in case no one believes it later. Dolores locks the door and waits for the final knock.

Title: The Coat with the Pistol
Cast: Wanda Merrick, Dolores Okonkwo, Walter Hargrove, Vernon Okonkwo
Plot: Lenore Merrick, a night-club coat check attendant, is handed a coat with a pistol in the pocket and a ticket stub for a train that left yesterday. The coat's owner, Wanda Delacroix, is the city's missing councillor, and the pistol is the one that killed the councillor's partner. Lenore is forced to make an unpopular choice about the coat with the pistol and faces the consequences alone. For one afternoon it seems that the coat with the pistol might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. The last shot is an empty office and a ringing telephone.

Title: The Burned Ledger
Cast: Lenore Sutterfield, Eleanor Ostrander, Hollis Wexcombe, Eleanor Lindqvist
Plot: Hollis Delacroix, a bank teller who is secretly a skilled forger, is blackmailed into copying a ledger that has already been burned. The original exists after all, and Dale Merrick, the blackmailer, wants the copy to be flawed in a very particular way. Over a long evening, Dale tells Hollis a story about the burned ledger that nobody else has heard. A week later, the burned ledger has cost Hollis a friendship and a good night's sleep. Hollis boards a night train under a new name.

Title: The Circus Restaurant
Cast: Unni Panicker, Unni Thulasidharan
Plot: Radhakrishnan Thampi, a tailor who inherits a circus, tries to turn the lion tamer's cage into a small restaurant. The lion, it turns out, refuses to leave, and Sreedevi Thampi, the cook, builds the entire menu around his appetite. The more Radhakrishnan learns about the circus restaurant, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. As the season turns, the circus restaurant becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Everything is resolved in a gloriously chaotic finale, and nobody is entirely forgiven.

Title: The Wedding Dress
Cast: Cora Sutterfield, Marcus Delacroix, Dale Sutterfield, Dale Okonkwo
Plot: Lenore Ostrander, a seamstress with a steady hand and a hidden debt, is hired to sew a wedding dress for the bride of a man Lenore once loved. Halfway through the fittings, Dale Merrick reveals that the bride knows everything and wants Lenore to stitch a message into the hem. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the wedding dress, and Lenore starts to suspect Dale. A week later, the wedding dress has cost Lenore a friendship and a good night's sleep. Lenore keeps coming back to the wedding dress, convinced that the answer is still there. Lenore leaves the old life behind, lighter and finally free.

Title: The Filmless Camera
Cast: Lorne Wharnecliffe, Duncan Lavoisy, Duncan Beaudrin, Gilles Gagnard
Plot: Marguerite Gagnard, a war photographer with a camera and no film, is ordered to document a battle for a newspaper that has already stopped printing. Hamish Lavoisy, a wounded sergeant, borrows the camera to record a last message, and the empty shutter clicks become the most honest record of the battle. Hamish warns that the filmless camera will ruin everyone involved, and Marguerite refuses to listen. Rumours about the filmless camera spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. A single cross marks the place where the unit made its stand.

Title: The Living Ink
Cast: Cora Pruitt, Lenore Lindqvist
Plot: Dolores Wexcombe, a mapmaker's apprentice, discovers that the ink in the master's workshop draws roads that did not exist the day before. Vernon Pruitt, the master, has been drawing a path to a hidden kingdom, and the ink will only dry once the journey is completed. As the season turns, the living ink becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Over a long evening, Vernon tells Dolores a story about the living ink that nobody else has heard. The old magic settles back into the hills, and the kingdom is whole again.

Title: The Goldfish Tunnel
Cast: Walter Pruitt, Eleanor Lindqvist, Dolores Pruitt
Plot: Hollis, a small fish who lives in a bowl, dreams of the ocean and begins to dig an escape tunnel through the water. Walter, a bowl-mate snail, points out that the bowl is the ocean as seen from the inside. Rumours about the goldfish tunnel spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Hollis thinks about the goldfish tunnel. Hollis keeps coming back to the goldfish tunnel, convinced that the answer is still there. The last scene is a long, happy sunrise with everybody still asleep.

Title: The Hollow Crown of Marsh End
Cast: Ambrose Quillfeather, Tabitha Merewether, Osric Ladbrooke
Plot: In the fen country of Marsh End, a farmer's daughter named Tansy Wickes finds a crown made of reeds floating down the flooded river and puts it on her head for a joke. Overnight the marsh begins to obey her: the mist thickens at her whisper, the eels escort her cattle home, and the long-drowned bell of a sunken village rings in the water. The crown, she learns from a travelling tinker, belongs to the Reed King, a spirit who ruled the fens before the drainage engineers arrived and who wants his kingdom back. Each time Tansy uses the crown, a little more of the village turns to marsh. The land agent who is trying to buy the farm schemes to drain the whole fen, and Tansy discovers that the crown can be used against him, at the price of her own name, which she begins to forget a syllable at a time. Her brother Alder, who cannot be sure whether she is still his sister, builds a raft and follows her into the deep marsh to bargain with the Reed King. The king offers to return everything the drainage took, the fields and the drowned church and the old fishing rights, if Tansy agrees to stay in the water as his queen. She negotiates a different bargain, trading the crown for a promise that the fens will be kept wet for seven generations and that no one will ever be drowned in them again. When she returns to the village, her name is whole and the marsh quietly withdraws, leaving a single reed on her pillow.

Title: Kimchi Wars
Cast: Han Do-yun, Oh Seul-bi, Jo Min-gyeom
Plot: Two rival kimchi vendors who have shared opposite stalls in a Busan market for thirty years are thrown into chaos when a television crew announces a national kimchi championship. Auntie Gyeong has a secret fermentation cellar and a famously bitter temper, while Auntie Pil has a recipe handed down from her grandmother and an army of cousins.
