Cast: Marcus Wexcombe, Eleanor Delacroix
Plot: Marcus Ostrander, a young florist, delivers a bouquet to a man in a hospital bed and finds it contains a coded demand written on the ribbon. The code is from Walter Hargrove, a hospital orderly who is blackmailing the man, and the florist's own shop is next on the list. For one afternoon it seems that the ribbon with the code might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. The more Marcus learns about the ribbon with the code, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Marcus boards a night train under a new name.

Title: The Delegates' Dialect
Cast: Burak Polatkan, Aylin Karabulut, Aylin Aksoylu
Plot: Aylin Tunçdemir, a conference interpreter, overhears two delegates speaking an obscure dialect and agreeing to a plan the other interpreters cannot understand. Deniz Yaşarel, the third speaker, is the only other person who understands, and makes Aylin an offer that is also a threat. Aylin is forced to make an unpopular choice about the delegates' dialect and faces the consequences alone. A week later, the delegates' dialect has cost Aylin a friendship and a good night's sleep. Aylin writes everything about the delegates' dialect down, in case no one believes it later. The closing shot reveals the true mastermind sitting calmly in the front row.

Title: Black Tulip Hotel
Cast: Fumiko Sakuradaira, Nobuyuki Tsugawara, Mitsuko Hayakeyama
Plot: A young travel writer named Aiko checks into a mountain inn in Nagano that is famous for the black tulips in its garden, flowers that supposedly bloom only once a decade. She finds that every other guest has the same room number on their keys, and that the innkeeper serves each of them the same meal at exactly the same moment. On her second night she follows the sound of a koto to a locked ballroom where the guests are dancing with their eyes closed. The innkeeper warns her to leave before the tulips bloom, but the road down the mountain has washed out.

Title: The Stopped Mantel Clock
Cast: Dolores Merrick, Eleanor Thibault, Walter Thibault, Walter Delacroix
Plot: Eleanor Pruitt, a clockmaker, is called to repair a mantel clock that has stopped at the exact minute of a death in the household.

Title: The Re-Locked Trunk
Cast: Walter Thibault, Walter Sutterfield, Eleanor Pruitt
Plot: Wanda Wexcombe, a diplomatic driver, notices that the car's trunk has been opened and re-locked a different way by someone in the embassy. Inside is Lenore Hargrove, the missing translator, alive and begging to be driven across the border without a word. For one afternoon it seems that the re-locked trunk might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. A week later, the re-locked trunk has cost Wanda a friendship and a good night's sleep. With seconds left, Wanda cuts the one wire that matters.

Title: The Scratched Wardrobe
Cast: Lata Vaidya, Aravind Vaidya, Aravind Bhosekar
Plot: Anjali Ranadive, a second-hand furniture dealer, buys a wardrobe whose inner back panel is covered in tally marks scratched from the inside. The tally marks continue to appear, one for each night, and Rohit Kolhatkar, the previous owner, begs Anjali to burn the wardrobe before the count reaches forty. Anjali writes everything about the scratched wardrobe down, in case no one believes it later. Anjali keeps coming back to the scratched wardrobe, convinced that the answer is still there. The last frame reveals that the danger has simply moved on to the next door.

Title: The Shipping-Notice Misspellings
Cast: Sunita Chitnis, Anjali Moitra, Kabir Sengupta
Plot: Meenal Sengupta, a newspaper proofreader, notices a pattern of misspellings in the shipping notices that always appear before a robbery. The misspellings are a code written by Lata Joglekar, the editor, who is hiding in plain sight as the gang's messenger. The more Meenal learns about the shipping-notice misspellings, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Meenal writes everything about the shipping-notice misspellings down, in case no one believes it later. Meenal boards a night train under a new name.

Title: The Landslide Week
Cast: Svetlana Dobrolyubov, Pavel Tomashevsky
Plot: Dmitri Tomashevsky, a cheese-maker in an alpine valley, meets a stranded cyclist who arrives during a landslide and cannot leave for a week. Natalya Orlov, the cyclist, is running from a wedding, and turns out to be the person Dmitri's family has been trying to arrange a marriage with. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Dmitri thinks about the landslide week. For one afternoon it seems that the landslide week might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Over a long evening, Natalya tells Dmitri a story about the landslide week that nobody else has heard. They part tenderly, promising to meet in the spring.

Title: The First Floating Lesson
Cast: Thankamma Kurup, Sreedevi Warrier, Gopan Warrier
Plot: Thankamma Thampi, a lifeguard at an indoor pool, is asked to teach an elderly swimmer who is afraid of water to float. Sreedevi Panicker, the swimmer, is the one who once rescued Thankamma's parent from the sea, and asks only to float once more. Thankamma is forced to make an unpopular choice about the first floating lesson and faces the consequences alone. For one afternoon it seems that the first floating lesson might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Sreedevi warns that the first floating lesson will ruin everyone involved, and Thankamma refuses to listen. The two begin again in a small house by the sea.

Title: The Midnight Bread
Cast: Hollis Sutterfield, Marcus Lindqvist, Eleanor Pruitt
Plot: Dolores Ostrander, a hospital cleaner on the cancer ward, starts teaching the patients to bake bread in a disused sluice room at three in the morning. A new administrator, Cora Wexcombe, threatens to close the room, unaware that the oven has become the only reason some patients stay. For one afternoon it seems that the midnight bread might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. A week later, the midnight bread has cost Dolores a friendship and a good night's sleep. The community gathers, and a quiet reconciliation settles over the final scene.

Title: Glass Harvest
Cast: Brindley Costain, Tamsin Yarrowood, Kelvin Dunmore
Plot: After eleven years without rain, the cattle station town of Mulga Flat survives by growing food inside towers of recycled glass that harvest fog from the desert night. Teenage engineer Ivy Corrigan keeps the towers running with spare parts and stubbornness, until a government survey team announces that the aquifer feeding the fog collectors is a fraud: the water has been piped in secretly from a mining company in exchange for silence. The mining company wants the town to stay dependent and quiet. Ivy discovers that the glass towers have been slowly changing colour each night, recording a pattern that matches seismic readings from the mine. She works out that the company's blasting is cracking the aquifer, and that the water it has been selling back to the town is the town's own. The survey team wants to evacuate everyone before the tower foundations fail, but nobody will leave without the harvest. Ivy organises a night shift that dismantles the towers panel by panel and rebuilds them on the shores of a salt lake sixty kilometres north. During the move, a dust storm traps a convoy of children in the old tower at the centre of town, and Ivy has to climb its failing frame to open the roof vents before the glass panels give way. In the final scene the first rain in eleven years falls on a ring of half-built towers and a crowd that has finally stopped counting. The credits roll over a long shot of the abandoned town, its empty glass towers catching the sunrise one panel at a time.

Title: The First Portraits
Cast: Walter Hargrove, Dale Sutterfield, Dolores Pruitt, Dolores Okonkwo
Plot: Vernon Lindqvist, a travelling photographer, sets up a studio in a town where no one has ever seen a picture of themselves. The first portrait shows Dolores Okonkwo, the pillar of the community, standing beside a man who is supposed to be dead. For one afternoon it seems that the first portraits might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Vernon is forced to make an unpopular choice about the first portraits and faces the consequences alone. Vernon hangs up the gun belt and stays on the porch.

Title: The Long Taxi Ride
Cast: Dale Pruitt, Marcus Hargrove, Dale Hargrove
Plot: Eleanor Merrick, a taxi driver who has never left the city, agrees to drive a dying stranger to see the sea three hundred kilometres away. At the coast, Marcus Wexcombe admits to having stolen the fare from the stranger's own estate, and begs Eleanor not to say a word. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the long taxi ride, and Eleanor starts to suspect Marcus. Nobody agrees on what the long taxi ride really means, least of all Marcus. Over a long evening, Marcus tells Eleanor a story about the long taxi ride that nobody else has heard. Eleanor leaves the old life behind, lighter and finally free.

Title: The Drifting Capsule
Cast: Dolores Sutterfield, Cora Wexcombe, Dolores Lindqvist, Lenore Ostrander
Plot: Wanda Hargrove, a retired astronaut with a failing heart, is asked to pilot one last mission to retrieve a capsule drifting past the orbit of Jupiter. The capsule holds a letter from Dolores Lindqvist, the astronaut's own younger self, sent forward in time and addressed to the same pilot. Late at night, Wanda finds one last clue about the drifting capsule that had been overlooked from the start. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the drifting capsule, and Wanda starts to suspect Dolores. The survivors set a new course toward a star nobody has named.

Title: The Stranded Station Quartet
Cast: Eun-ji Yoon, Min-jun Seo, Hye-jin Seo
Plot: So-ra Seo, a railway porter, assembles a jazz quartet of travellers stranded in a snowbound station. Min-jun Baek, the stationmaster, owns a legendary trumpet in the lost-property room, and decides that tonight is the night to play it. As the season turns, the stranded station quartet becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. A week later, the stranded station quartet has cost So-ra a friendship and a good night's sleep. Rumours about the stranded station quartet spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. The festival becomes an annual tradition, with everyone in the key of their choice.

Title: The Torn-Tailed Kite
Cast: Hamish Wharnecliffe, Hamish Chapdelaine
Plot: Duncan, a young paper kite with a torn tail, dreams of flying across the sea to see the place where the wind is born. Hamish, a gruff weathervane, offers directions, but warns that no kite has ever returned. Nobody agrees on what the torn-tailed kite really means, least of all Hamish. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Duncan thinks about the torn-tailed kite. Duncan finally reaches the end of the journey and giggles.

Title: The Dead Soldier's Confession
Cast: Sreedevi Thampi, Maya Warrier, Maya Thampi, Gopan Warrier
Plot: Radhakrishnan Panicker, a chaplain on a troop ship, listens to the confession of a soldier who claims to have died two weeks earlier. Vijayan Thampi, the ship's doctor, confirms the death certificate, and the chaplain must decide which of them is mistaken. Nobody agrees on what the dead soldier's confession really means, least of all Vijayan. Late at night, Radhakrishnan finds one last clue about the dead soldier's confession that had been overlooked from the start. Radhakrishnan keeps coming back to the dead soldier's confession, convinced that the answer is still there. Radhakrishnan returns home to a town that has already moved on.

Title: The Flea-Market Lamp
Cast: Dale Wexcombe, Eleanor Merrick, Dale Hargrove, Walter Lindqvist
Plot: Hollis, a little lamp in a flea market, wishes to light a window instead of a shelf. Walter, a lonely child, buys the lamp for a single coin, and the two light an attic until dawn. Walter warns that the flea-market lamp will ruin everyone involved, and Hollis refuses to listen. For one afternoon it seems that the flea-market lamp might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Nobody agrees on what the flea-market lamp really means, least of all Walter. The last scene is a long, happy sunrise with everybody still asleep.

Title: The Violin Case
Cast: Mei Yip, Yee Yip, Siu Yip
Plot: Lan Tsui, a child evacuated from a bombed city, carries a violin case containing a loaf of bread and a letter. The letter is addressed to Chun Lo, a stranger in the countryside, and asks them to raise a child they have never met. Late at night, Lan finds one last clue about the violin case that had been overlooked from the start. Lan keeps coming back to the violin case, convinced that the answer is still there. Lan returns home to a town that has already moved on.

Title: The Shifting City Map
Cast: Marcus Pruitt, Wanda Pruitt, Lenore Merrick, Vernon Wexcombe
Plot: Hollis Pruitt, a city planner in a domed metropolis, discovers that the map of the streets is slowly rearranging itself at night. Walter Ostrander, the master architect, confesses that the dome was designed to confuse its inhabitants and keep them from leaving. Walter warns that the shifting city map will ruin everyone involved, and Hollis refuses to listen. Rumours about the shifting city map spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. The more Hollis learns about the shifting city map, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. A new horizon rises on the viewscreen, quiet and green.

Title: The Key to Nowhere
Cast: Wanda Delacroix, Wanda Hargrove, Dale Merrick, Dolores Hargrove
Plot: Walter Lindqvist, a young blacksmith, forges a key that does not fit any lock in the kingdom but opens a door in the air. Beyond the door is Marcus Thibault, the lost queen, waiting for a key that has been missing for three hundred years. Walter is forced to make an unpopular choice about the key to nowhere and faces the consequences alone. Late at night, Walter finds one last clue about the key to nowhere that had been overlooked from the start. The final spell is spoken in a whisper, and the world quietly shifts.

Title: The Burning Toll Coin
Cast: Margery Haythorne, Imogen Tregenza, Neville Pemberton, Alistair Cholmondeley
Plot: Winifred Tregenza, a bridge toll collector on the night shift, takes a coin from a driver that is hot enough to burn. More and more coins arrive from empty cars, and Margery Haythorne, the toll supervisor, orders Winifred to keep a perfect count until morning. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Winifred thinks about the burning toll coin. Late at night, Winifred finds one last clue about the burning toll coin that had been overlooked from the start. A week later, the burning toll coin has cost Winifred a friendship and a good night's sleep. Only a recording of the final hour remains, and nobody dares to play it.

Title: The Four Dark Minutes
Cast: Dolores Pruitt, Hollis Merrick, Dale Thibault
Plot: Hollis Pruitt, a lighthouse mechanic, is paid in cash to shut off the beam for exactly four minutes on a foggy night. Vernon Wexcombe, the client, is landing a boat on the rocks, and the mechanic must decide who gets to survive the next storm. Hollis keeps coming back to the four dark minutes, convinced that the answer is still there. As the season turns, the four dark minutes becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Hollis writes everything about the four dark minutes down, in case no one believes it later. The city goes on as it always does, with its lights low and its secrets high.

Title: The Glowing Sheep
Cast: Karthikeyan Annamalai, Revathi Natarajan
Plot: Kalyani Annamalai, a shepherd on a cloud-covered mountain, finds a sheep whose wool glows with the stories it has heard. Murugesan Ayyadurai, a travelling bard, offers a fortune for a single fleece, and the sheep begins to tell the bard's own story back to the bard. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the glowing sheep, and Kalyani starts to suspect Murugesan. Kalyani writes everything about the glowing sheep down, in case no one believes it later. The more Kalyani learns about the glowing sheep, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. The final spell is spoken in a whisper, and the world quietly shifts.

Title: The Suit-Lining Account Numbers
Cast: Marcus Wexcombe, Cora Sutterfield, Marcus Hargrove
Plot: Vernon Wexcombe, the owner of a failing tailor shop, discovers that the linings of the suits left for alteration are stitched with account numbers. Hollis Hargrove, a customer who never collects the suit, is using the shop as a bank, and the police now want to know what Vernon knows. Nobody agrees on what the suit-lining account numbers really means, least of all Hollis. Rumours about the suit-lining account numbers spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. A week later, the suit-lining account numbers has cost Vernon a friendship and a good night's sleep. The money is never found, and the city quietly changes hands.

Title: The Drover's Hymn
Cast: Cecil Mulgrave, Ngaire Tolhurst, Dougal Ashcroft
Plot: In 1890s Queensland, a widowed drover named Hannah Cobb takes a mob of two thousand cattle across the Barkly Tableland to a railhead nine hundred kilometres away, with nothing but a limping dog, a teenage stockman and a wagon of hymn books. The station owner who hired her has secretly sold the cattle twice and plans to leave her stranded with the debt. Along the way she negotiates with the Mitakoodi elders for access to a waterhole, and learns that the land she has been driving across is the subject of a forgotten treaty. When a bushfire cuts the route, Hannah must decide whether to abandon the herd or lead it through the burning grass at night.

Title: The Arctic Seed Vault
Cast: Eleanor Thibault, Wanda Lindqvist
Plot: Cora Delacroix, a seed vault guardian beneath an arctic ice cap, is told to destroy the collection by a government that has stopped paying the electric bill. Dolores Okonkwo, a young soldier sent to enforce the order, secretly plants a handful of seeds in a coat pocket. The more Cora learns about the arctic seed vault, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Late at night, Cora finds one last clue about the arctic seed vault that had been overlooked from the start. Cora transmits the truth to everyone who can still hear it.

Title: The Geese Uprising
Cast: Imogen Tregenza, Margery Ashworth, Alistair Ashworth, Philippa Bramwell
Plot: Winifred Quayle, a goose girl, learns to speak the language of the wild geese, and hears them plan an uprising against the king. Philippa Bramwell, the king, is secretly a goose, and begs the girl to translate on the king's behalf. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the geese uprising, and Winifred starts to suspect Philippa. Winifred keeps coming back to the geese uprising, convinced that the answer is still there. Rumours about the geese uprising spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. The old magic settles back into the hills, and the kingdom is whole again.

Title: The Replaced Map
Cast: Devendra Dhawalkar, Meenal Ranadive, Aravind Bhosekar, Nandini Vaidya
Plot: Sunita Vaidya, a village librarian, notices that a rare map has been cut from an atlas and replaced with a perfect drawing. The drawing was made by Devendra Vaidya, a respected local historian, who needed the original to prove a claim about a vanished parish. The more Sunita learns about the replaced map, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Sunita writes everything about the replaced map down, in case no one believes it later. As the season turns, the replaced map becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. In the drawing room, Sunita gathers the suspects and finally explains.

Title: The Letter to an Unknown Planet
Cast: Trevor Ironbridge, Bruce Tolhurst, Narelle Ironbridge
Plot: Clive Mulgrave, an interstellar mail carrier, is assigned a letter that must be delivered to a planet that has not yet been discovered. The sender, Trevor Pemberthy, is already waiting on the planet when Clive arrives, and they have been dead for a thousand years. Late at night, Clive finds one last clue about the letter to an unknown planet that had been overlooked from the start. Trevor warns that the letter to an unknown planet will ruin everyone involved, and Clive refuses to listen. Rumours about the letter to an unknown planet spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. The machine is switched off, but its last question remains unanswered.

Title: The Single Nightly Note
Cast: Alistair Haythorne, Margery Quayle, Beatrice Cholmondeley
Plot: Neville Fairweather, a night-school pianist, learns that the practice room on the third floor is booked every night by someone who plays only one note. Gethin Quayle, the other pianist, plays only the first note of a song they cannot finish, and waits for Neville to supply the second. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Neville thinks about the single nightly note. Nobody agrees on what the single nightly note really means, least of all Gethin. A week later, the single nightly note has cost Neville a friendship and a good night's sleep. A final kiss closes the season.

Title: The Friday Winnings
Cast: Marguerite Lavoisy, Gilles Chapdelaine, Solange Wharnecliffe, Hamish Wharnecliffe
Plot: Marguerite Charbonnet, a night-shift cashier at a racetrack, notices that one bettor wins exactly the same amount every Friday. The winner is Gilles Gagnard, a retired judge, who is laundering the sentences once handed down from the bench by paying out other people's debts. The more Marguerite learns about the Friday winnings, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Marguerite writes everything about the Friday winnings down, in case no one believes it later. Rumours about the Friday winnings spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. Marguerite boards a night train under a new name.

Title: The Funeral for the Living
Cast: Takeshi Mizoguro, Kimiko Hakamadajima, Daisuke Tachibara
Plot: Michiko Tachibara, a jazz bassist with a gambling problem, is asked to play at a funeral for a man who is still sitting in the front pew. Haruto Aokawa, the supposed corpse, has staged a death to flush out a partner, and needs the bassist to keep playing. The more Michiko learns about the funeral for the living, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Haruto warns that the funeral for the living will ruin everyone involved, and Michiko refuses to listen. Michiko writes everything about the funeral for the living down, in case no one believes it later. The city goes on as it always does, with its lights low and its secrets high.

Title: The Island at Low Tide
Cast: Yuki Mizoguro, Sakura Hayakeyama, Kimiko Aokawa, Daisuke Aokawa
Plot: Michiko Ishizumi, a lighthouse keeper on an island that appears only at low tide, receives a ship that has not sunk yet. Kimiko Tsugawara, the ship's captain, has come to ask the keeper to put out the light, so the wreck can be avoided, and Michiko must choose. A week later, the island at low tide has cost Michiko a friendship and a good night's sleep. As the season turns, the island at low tide becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. The door closes, but the key stays in Michiko's pocket.

Title: The Permanent Passenger
Cast: Marguerite Beaudrin, Duncan Beaudrin
Plot: Lorne Lavoisy, a ferry deckhand on a lake in winter, discovers a passenger who has been sitting in the same seat since the vessel was launched. The passenger, Mireille Charbonnet, asks only to be taken to the far shore, where Lorne's father drowned, and where the ice is thin. Over a long evening, Mireille tells Lorne a story about the permanent passenger that nobody else has heard. Lorne keeps coming back to the permanent passenger, convinced that the answer is still there. Lorne locks the door and waits for the final knock.

Title: The Dry Cloud
Cast: Kalyani Ayyadurai, Revathi Velusamy, Senthil Sivakumaran, Senthil Velusamy
Plot: Senthil, a tiny cloud who cannot rain, drifts into a drought-stricken valley. Pandian, an old farmer, teaches the cloud to rain by telling it a joke. Nobody agrees on what the dry cloud really means, least of all Pandian. Senthil finally reaches the end of the journey and giggles.

Title: The Concert Ticket
Cast: Lakshmi Velusamy, Karthikeyan Sivakumaran, Kalyani Sivakumaran, Pandian Sivakumaran
Plot: Kalyani Ayyadurai, a locksmith asked to open a safe in a dead stranger's apartment, finds it already empty except for a ticket to a concert that has not happened yet. Vasanthi Chidambaram, a crooked police sergeant, has been waiting for the safe to be opened so that the ticket can be traded to the right buyer. Nobody agrees on what the concert ticket really means, least of all Vasanthi. Kalyani is forced to make an unpopular choice about the concert ticket and faces the consequences alone. Over a long evening, Vasanthi tells Kalyani a story about the concert ticket that nobody else has heard. Kalyani boards a night train under a new name.

Title: The Burned-Theatre Opera
Cast: Eleanor Pruitt, Vernon Thibault, Wanda Sutterfield, Marcus Hargrove
Plot: Lenore Pruitt, a village schoolteacher, trains a class of fifteen students to perform an opera in the ruins of a burned theatre. Wanda Pruitt, a parent, brings the single surviving costume from the original production, and the children refuse to perform without it. For one afternoon it seems that the burned-theatre opera might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Wanda warns that the burned-theatre opera will ruin everyone involved, and Lenore refuses to listen. The more Lenore learns about the burned-theatre opera, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Lenore takes a final bow under the old marquee.

Title: The Ticket to Nowhere
Cast: Kimiko Ishizumi, Yuki Tsugawara, Daisuke Aokawa
Plot: Takeshi Aokawa, a night-train conductor, falls for a passenger who always buys a ticket to a station that does not exist. Haruto Tachibara, the passenger, admits that the destination is the place where the pair first met, and asks the conductor to invent it. Over a long evening, Haruto tells Takeshi a story about the ticket to nowhere that nobody else has heard. Takeshi writes everything about the ticket to nowhere down, in case no one believes it later. A final kiss closes the season.

Title: Tin Soldiers of Avenue Dorval
Cast: Voices of Aurelie Bergevin, Nestor Chapdelaine, Cosette Lamouche
Plot: In a cluttered attic above a Montreal toy shop, a regiment of tin soldiers wakes each night to hold parade for an audience of dust motes and one patient spider. When a little girl named Josette leaves a broken music box on the staircase, Sergeant Alphonse leads a rescue mission through the shop's cardboard canyons to repair it before the shop owner returns. They must cross a river of spilled marbles, outwit a prowling cat named Napoleon, and persuade a stubborn porcelain ballerina to dance one last time so that the music box can play.

Title: The Ghostwritten Confession
Cast: Walter Thibault, Dolores Okonkwo
Plot: Vernon Pruitt, a failed novelist working as a ghostwriter for a crime boss, is asked to write the boss's confession. Every chapter incriminates Dale Okonkwo, the boss's lieutenant, and the writer realises the book is intended as a weapon. Vernon writes everything about the ghostwritten confession down, in case no one believes it later. Nobody agrees on what the ghostwritten confession really means, least of all Dale. The last shot is an empty office and a ringing telephone.

Title: The Dead Guest's Booking
Cast: Unni Thampi, Sreedevi Varyar
Plot: Sreedevi Varyar, a hotel concierge in a mountain resort, receives a booking in the name of a person who died decades ago. The guest arrives, and Maya Panicker, the old woman who checks in, hands Sreedevi an envelope that explains exactly why the hotel will be empty by morning. Late at night, Sreedevi finds one last clue about the dead guest's booking that had been overlooked from the start. Maya warns that the dead guest's booking will ruin everyone involved, and Sreedevi refuses to listen. Rumours about the dead guest's booking spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. The conspiracy collapses, and Sreedevi disappears from public life.

Title: The Misshelved Cookbook
Cast: Dong-hyun Bae, Hye-jin Baek, Min-jun Seo
Plot: Ji-ho Seo, the owner of a failing bookshop, discovers that the shop's only bestseller is a cookbook that was shelved in the wrong section. Eun-ji Oh, the author, arrives to complain, only to learn that every reader has been following the recipes backwards. Ji-ho writes everything about the misshelved cookbook down, in case no one believes it later. Late at night, Ji-ho finds one last clue about the misshelved cookbook that had been overlooked from the start. The whole town squeezes into one room for a deeply awkward reveal.

Title: The Warm Core Sample
Cast: Irina Rostovtsev, Natalya Kuznetsov, Irina Beloselsky
Plot: Dmitri Rostovtsev, a young geologist drilling core samples in a remote quarry, brings up a cylinder of rock that is warm to the touch. Each sample drilled afterward is warmer, and Natalya Rostovtsev, the foreman, refuses to stop the drilling because of a contract. A week later, the warm core sample has cost Dmitri a friendship and a good night's sleep. Dmitri is forced to make an unpopular choice about the warm core sample and faces the consequences alone. Dmitri survives until dawn, but something is still watching from the window.

Title: The Phantom Cab Address
Cast: Lenore Okonkwo, Marcus Merrick
Plot: Vernon Lindqvist, a night-shift dispatcher for autonomous cabs, notices that a single vehicle keeps taking passengers to an address that does not exist. The address appears when Wanda Lindqvist, the vehicle's final passenger, asks to be taken home, and Vernon finds the door open. A week later, the phantom cab address has cost Vernon a friendship and a good night's sleep. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Vernon thinks about the phantom cab address. The survivors set a new course toward a star nobody has named.

Title: The Premature Wake
Cast: Kimiko Hakamadajima, Yuki Aokawa, Kimiko Hayakeyama, Yuki Ishizumi
Plot: Shinji Ishizumi, an unemployed magician, is hired to entertain a retirement party that turns out to be a wake for a man who is still alive. The guest of honour, Takeshi Tachibara, joins the act, and the two stage a miraculous resurrection that nobody can explain afterwards. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the premature wake, and Shinji starts to suspect Takeshi. Takeshi warns that the premature wake will ruin everyone involved, and Shinji refuses to listen. The whole town squeezes into one room for a deeply awkward reveal.

Title: The Advice Column Pseudonym
Cast: Cora Ostrander, Wanda Wexcombe, Marcus Thibault, Vernon Ostrander
Plot: Marcus Pruitt, a paperboy-turned-journalist, writes weekly love advice in a newspaper under a false name. Walter Okonkwo, the editor, replies in print to every column, and the town begins reading them as a public correspondence. A week later, the advice column pseudonym has cost Marcus a friendship and a good night's sleep. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Marcus thinks about the advice column pseudonym. Nobody agrees on what the advice column pseudonym really means, least of all Walter. The two begin again in a small house by the sea.

Title: The Empty Farmhouse Line
Cast: Eleanor Thibault, Wanda Merrick, Vernon Hargrove
Plot: Marcus Ostrander, a village telephone operator, is told by an advancing army to connect every call to a number that rings in an empty farmhouse. Hollis Hargrove, the farmhouse's hidden occupant, answers every call and quietly passes information in the other direction. Rumours about the empty farmhouse line spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. Marcus writes everything about the empty farmhouse line down, in case no one believes it later. The more Marcus learns about the empty farmhouse line, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. A single cross marks the place where the unit made its stand.

Title: The Campfire Song from the Lake
Cast: Sakura Mizoguro, Takeshi Hayakeyama, Shinji Ishizumi
Plot: Shinji Ishizumi, a camp counsellor, hears the old campfire song sung by a choir of voices from the middle of the lake. Every verse ends with the name of a child who has not arrived yet, and Michiko Ishizumi, the camp director, has been writing those names on the cabin doors. Rumours about the campfire song from the lake spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. A week later, the campfire song from the lake has cost Shinji a friendship and a good night's sleep. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the campfire song from the lake, and Shinji starts to suspect Michiko. Only a recording of the final hour remains, and nobody dares to play it.

Title: The First-Love Music Box
Cast: Bruce Pemberthy, Narelle Dunmore, Gary Dunmore, Trevor Pemberthy
Plot: Kerry Mulgrave, an apprentice at a music-box factory, begins to compose a tune that makes people remember their first love. Shelley Costain, the owner, mass-produces the box, and the tune becomes a sign that Kerry's own love was never returned. Nobody agrees on what the first-love music box really means, least of all Shelley. Kerry keeps coming back to the first-love music box, convinced that the answer is still there. Kerry delivers the closing number without a trace of nerves.

Title: The Burnt Birthday Cake
Cast: Aravind Bhosekar, Rohit Chitnis, Kabir Pandharkar, Devendra Sengupta
Plot: Rohit, a pocket-sized dragon, accidentally burns the town's only birthday cake and sets out to bake another. Vikrant, a stern fairy baker, supplies the recipe, but demands that the dragon learn to cook without breathing fire. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Rohit thinks about the burnt birthday cake. For one afternoon it seems that the burnt birthday cake might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. The last scene is a long, happy sunrise with everybody still asleep.

Title: The Covered-Lamp Boat
Cast: Eleanor Pruitt, Marcus Pruitt
Plot: Dale Delacroix, a coastal lookout, spots a fishing boat that makes the same crossing each night with its lamp covered. Walter Delacroix, the fisherman, is carrying refugees in the hold, and begs the lookout to keep reporting nothing. As the season turns, the covered-lamp boat becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Dale is forced to make an unpopular choice about the covered-lamp boat and faces the consequences alone. In the last shot, a line of figures walks across an open field toward the sound of church bells.

Title: The Tended Grave
Cast: Alistair Bramwell, Rupert Bramwell
Plot: Margery Tregenza, the caretaker of a hilltop cemetery, begins receiving monthly payments from an unknown sender to keep one particular grave free of weeds. Margery follows the trail of money to Imogen Haythorne, a prosperous stranger who has been paying for a grave that holds nothing at all. As the season turns, the tended grave becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. A week later, the tended grave has cost Margery a friendship and a good night's sleep. The last shot is an ordinary morning, with nothing and everything changed.

Title: The Seven-Minute Clock
Cast: Irina Beloselsky, Olga Rostovtsev
Plot: Dmitri Orlov, a train station clock-winder, learns that the town's famous clock has been wrong by exactly seven minutes for forty years. Anatoly Orlov, the retired winder, admits that the error was intentional, so that two lovers might always arrive in time. The more Dmitri learns about the seven-minute clock, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. For one afternoon it seems that the seven-minute clock might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Dmitri thinks about the seven-minute clock. They part tenderly, promising to meet in the spring.

Title: The Locked Vault
Cast: Eleanor Sutterfield, Vernon Okonkwo
Plot: Cora Pruitt, a retired safecracker, is dragged out of retirement when an old rival is found dead inside a vault that was locked from the outside. The only way to open the door without a key is to use one of Cora's own techniques, and Vernon Thibault, the detective, is quietly counting on it. Cora is forced to make an unpopular choice about the locked vault and faces the consequences alone. A week later, the locked vault has cost Cora a friendship and a good night's sleep. Cora walks away with nothing but a clean name.

Title: The Robber's Portrait
Cast: Margery Cholmondeley, Winifred Pemberton, Margery Haythorne, Alistair Tregenza
Plot: Edmund Tregenza, a street portrait artist in a casino town, is asked to sketch the face of a man who has just robbed a vault. Gethin Thackeray, the detective, realises the sketch is a perfect likeness of a policeman, and begins to doubt the entire investigation. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the robber's portrait, and Edmund starts to suspect Gethin. Edmund keeps coming back to the robber's portrait, convinced that the answer is still there. A week later, the robber's portrait has cost Edmund a friendship and a good night's sleep. Edmund boards a night train under a new name.

Title: The Wounded Sniper
Cast: Edmund Ashworth, Edmund Bramwell, Philippa Bramwell, Edmund Lockhart
Plot: Imogen Pemberton, a nurse in a field hospital, is forced to treat a wounded enemy sniper in a tent full of his victims. Margery Haythorne, a patient who is also the sniper's former neighbour, asks for the sniper's name and then asks the nurse to forget it. Nobody agrees on what the wounded sniper really means, least of all Margery. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Imogen thinks about the wounded sniper. In the last shot, a line of figures walks across an open field toward the sound of church bells.

Title: The Ruined Festival
Cast: Dolores Okonkwo, Wanda Ostrander, Lenore Thibault, Cora Sutterfield
Plot: Cora Wexcombe, a weather forecaster who has been wrong for twenty years, is blamed when a town's entire annual festival is rained out. Vernon Wexcombe, the festival organiser, notices that the forecasts are wrong in a perfectly predictable direction, and hires Cora as an oracle. Cora is forced to make an unpopular choice about the ruined festival and faces the consequences alone. As the season turns, the ruined festival becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Everything is resolved in a gloriously chaotic finale, and nobody is entirely forgiven.

Title: The Cellar Surgery
Cast: Nandini Chitnis, Kabir Sengupta, Rohit Sengupta, Sunita Dhawalkar
Plot: Meenal Dhawalkar, a surgeon operating by candlelight in a cellar, realises that the patient is the commander of the army that has just shelled the town. Nandini Bhosekar, the surgeon's assistant, holds a pistol and says only that the operation should not be too successful. As the season turns, the cellar surgery becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Over a long evening, Nandini tells Meenal a story about the cellar surgery that nobody else has heard. Meenal is forced to make an unpopular choice about the cellar surgery and faces the consequences alone. A single cross marks the place where the unit made its stand.

Title: The Newborn's Lantern
Cast: Lata Joglekar, Kabir Moitra, Anjali Dhawalkar
Plot: Aravind Moitra, a village midwife, delivers a child who is born holding a tiny, working lantern. Vikrant Sengupta, the lantern's maker, arrives from under the hills to claim the child as an apprentice, and the village must decide what to pay. Aravind writes everything about the newborn's lantern down, in case no one believes it later. A week later, the newborn's lantern has cost Aravind a friendship and a good night's sleep. The more Aravind learns about the newborn's lantern, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. The door closes, but the key stays in Aravind's pocket.

Title: Atlas of Lost Birthdays
Cast: Yoon Chae-rin, Kwon Ji-hoon, Baek Na-ra
Plot: Every birthday that is not celebrated disappears from the calendar and drifts to a hidden city called Hanyeol, where a clerk named Mira catalogues them in an enormous atlas. When a lonely thirty-year-old accountant, Do-yeon, discovers that her missing birthdays have been stacked on a shelf in Mira's archive, she travels there on the last train of a rainy night. The city is built from lost candles, uneaten cakes and unsent greeting cards, and it is slowly running out of space. Mira admits that no one has ever returned a birthday to its owner, because the rules say that each one has to be celebrated by a stranger before it can leave. Do-yeon sets out to collect thirty strangers willing to celebrate with her, beginning with a ticket inspector, a one-eyed baker and a child who has never had a party. Each celebration is strange and hesitant, and each gives her back a year. Along the way she learns that the atlas itself is made from the birthdays no one ever claimed, and that Mira is the first of them, the birthday of a girl who was never born. At the last party, with only Mira remaining on the list, Do-yeon decides to give the final year away and bake a cake for the clerk. The atlas opens at an empty page, and Mira walks out of the city into a morning where the calendar has quietly added her name. In the closing scene, Do-yeon finds on her own doorstep a small parcel tied with string, and inside it is a candle. The atlas is still there, they say, but the shelf where her years were kept has been given over to a window.

Title: The Two-Hundred-Year Distress Call
Cast: Yuki Tsugawara, Michiko Tsugawara, Takeshi Hayakeyama, Yuki Hayakeyama
Plot: Kimiko Tachibara, a mining-drone pilot on an asteroid belt, picks up a distress signal from a ship that was lost two hundred years ago. The ship is intact and crewed by Haruto Hakamadajima, who greets Kimiko by name and explains that the voyage has been waiting for exactly this arrival. Kimiko keeps coming back to the two-hundred-year distress call, convinced that the answer is still there. Nobody agrees on what the two-hundred-year distress call really means, least of all Haruto. Kimiko is forced to make an unpopular choice about the two-hundred-year distress call and faces the consequences alone. A new horizon rises on the viewscreen, quiet and green.

Title: Midnight Ferry to Kowloon
Cast: Tsui Man-kei, Fong Ka-yee, Chow Sin-lok
Plot: Customs inspector Lau Tak-wing boards the last Star Ferry of the night carrying a sealed envelope that proves his superior is smuggling. Within minutes he realises that two passengers are following him, and that the ferry's engineer has been paid to stop the boat in the middle of the harbour. With forty minutes until the next crossing, Lau must hand off the envelope to a stranger, a sleepy nurse, without explaining why, and then keep both pursuers busy on deck.

Title: The Unlisted Village
Cast: Natalya Orlov, Olga Rostovtsev
Plot: Anatoly Orlov, a bus passenger on a long night route, notices that the driver stops at a village that does not appear on any timetable. Pavel Orlov, an elderly woman who gets off there, leaves a ticket on the seat for Anatoly with the date of a return journey that has already passed. Pavel warns that the unlisted village will ruin everyone involved, and Anatoly refuses to listen. Anatoly is forced to make an unpopular choice about the unlisted village and faces the consequences alone. Anatoly locks the door and waits for the final knock.

Title: Dust Over Cinder Creek
Cast: Vernon Calloway, Wanda Merrick, Jasper Okonkwo
Plot: Sheriff Amos Reed has one week left before retirement when a stranger rides into Cinder Creek with a wounded boy and a map to a buried strongbox. The town's banker wants the map; so does a gang that has been trailing the stranger across three territories. Reed must decide whether to hand the boy over to men with legal papers or to hide him in the church bell tower and face the gang alone at sunset.

Title: Seven Days of Rain in Tsarskoye
Cast: Evgenia Rostovtsova, Kirill Dobrolyubov, Anfisa Verbitskaya
Plot: A stationmaster's wife in a provincial town waits for a train that has not arrived in seven days of continuous rain, and the passengers stranded on the platform slowly reveal their secrets to each other. A student carries a forged letter of introduction; a soldier is going home to a village that no longer exists; a priest has lost his faith. By the seventh night the waiting room has become a kind of confessional, and the stationmaster's wife begins to wonder whether she wants the train to arrive at all.

Title: The Stolen Violin
Cast: Cora Thibault, Dolores Delacroix, Cora Sutterfield, Cora Pruitt
Plot: Walter Hargrove, a pawnshop owner, buys a violin that turns out to be the missing centrepiece of a heist from a decade ago. Marcus Lindqvist, the thief, returns to buy it back at ten times the price, and refuses to say why the violin is worth more silent than played. As the season turns, the stolen violin becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. A week later, the stolen violin has cost Walter a friendship and a good night's sleep. Walter boards a night train under a new name.

Title: The Unexplained Figure in the Photographs
Cast: Mireille Lavoisy, Lorne Beaudrin, Duncan Wharnecliffe
Plot: Marguerite Charbonnet, a seaside photographer, develops a roll of film from a tourist who has disappeared and finds a figure in every frame. The figure is Lorne Beaudrin, a local fisherman, who appears in the background of every picture because the fisherman was following the tourist. Marguerite keeps coming back to the unexplained figure in the photographs, convinced that the answer is still there. For one afternoon it seems that the unexplained figure in the photographs might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. In the drawing room, Marguerite gathers the suspects and finally explains.

Title: The Rally Driving Car
Cast: Marcus Okonkwo, Eleanor Wexcombe, Vernon Okonkwo
Plot: Cora Okonkwo, a mild-mannered driving instructor, discovers that the car used for lessons has been accidentally entered into a cross-country rally. Hollis Delacroix, the rally organiser, refuses to believe the entry was a mistake and assigns Cora a navigator who cannot read maps. Late at night, Cora finds one last clue about the rally driving car that had been overlooked from the start. A week later, the rally driving car has cost Cora a friendship and a good night's sleep. Cora keeps coming back to the rally driving car, convinced that the answer is still there. The film ends with a toast, a collapsed table and a very large cake.

Title: The Boot-Sized Nugget
Cast: Rupert Ashworth, Alistair Haythorne, Edmund Tregenza
Plot: Alistair Pemberton, a gold prospector who has not struck colour in nine years, finds a nugget the size of a boot lodged in a creek bed. Winifred Fairweather, the claim jumper, has been following Alistair for years in the hope of exactly this, and offers an unexpected partnership. The more Alistair learns about the boot-sized nugget, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. A week later, the boot-sized nugget has cost Alistair a friendship and a good night's sleep. Alistair is forced to make an unpopular choice about the boot-sized nugget and faces the consequences alone. The town has a new law and an old grudge buried deep in the ground.

Title: The National Choir Prize
Cast: Dolores Pruitt, Cora Okonkwo, Marcus Thibault, Lenore Okonkwo
Plot: Dolores Thibault, a village blacksmith with a booming voice, is drafted into a choir competing for a national prize. Lenore Okonkwo, the conductor, wants only to hear Dolores's voice in a single note, and builds the entire anthem around that one phrase. Over a long evening, Lenore tells Dolores a story about the national choir prize that nobody else has heard. Nobody agrees on what the national choir prize really means, least of all Lenore. The festival becomes an annual tradition, with everyone in the key of their choice.

Title: The Moved Signal Lever
Cast: Anjali Ranadive, Sunita Chitnis, Nandini Ranadive, Rohit Sengupta
Plot: Vikrant Vaidya, a train signaller, finds that a signal lever has been moved by an unknown hand to send two express trains toward each other. Kabir Joglekar, a fellow signaller, has locked the cabin door from outside and left a note explaining that a third train is the actual target. Late at night, Vikrant finds one last clue about the moved signal lever that had been overlooked from the start. Kabir warns that the moved signal lever will ruin everyone involved, and Vikrant refuses to listen. Vikrant survives, though the evidence is never recovered.

Title: Cold Storage
Cast: Thalia Bourgouin, Ewan Ferrington, Lucette Charbonnet
Plot: The night-shift supervisor of a frozen-food warehouse outside Winnipeg, Cal Ferris, begins to find boxes of fish that have been rearranged overnight into patterns he cannot explain. A temperature alarm sounds in a freezer that has been empty for years, and when Cal opens the door he finds a single chair facing the wall. His two coworkers dismiss it as a prank until the security cameras show a figure walking between the racks at a pace too slow to be human. They lock themselves in the break room as the temperature outside the door falls below minus forty.

Title: The Sea Monster Costume
Cast: Cem Karabulut, Deniz Aksoylu, Burak Özdilek
Plot: Burak Polatkan, a fishmonger with a theatrical streak, is cast by mistake as the lead in a local opera about a sea monster. Aylin Tunçdemir, the director, writes the monster a whole new aria after hearing Burak's accidental falsetto in the dress rehearsal. As the season turns, the sea monster costume becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Burak is forced to make an unpopular choice about the sea monster costume and faces the consequences alone. For one afternoon it seems that the sea monster costume might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. The film ends with a toast, a collapsed table and a very large cake.

Title: The Last Water Well
Cast: Vernon Wexcombe, Lenore Merrick
Plot: Vernon Delacroix, a rancher's widow, hires a blind gunslinger to protect the last remaining water well. Hollis Pruitt, the gunslinger, has memorised the footsteps of every rider in the valley, and uses the knowledge to expose the traitor in the household. Vernon keeps coming back to the last water well, convinced that the answer is still there. Late at night, Vernon finds one last clue about the last water well that had been overlooked from the start. As the season turns, the last water well becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. The town has a new law and an old grudge buried deep in the ground.

Title: The Phantom Tea Orders
Cast: Kemal Tunçdemir, Emre Yaşarel, Burak Tunçdemir, Kemal Karabulut
Plot: Emre Polatkan, a tea shop owner, receives a daily order from an address that burned down fifteen years ago. Selin Yaşarel, the only survivor of the fire, has been using the orders to signal that the cause was not an accident. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Emre thinks about the phantom tea orders. For one afternoon it seems that the phantom tea orders might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. Late at night, Emre finds one last clue about the phantom tea orders that had been overlooked from the start. The case is closed, though the last clue remains in Emre's pocket.

Title: The Rearranged Diary
Cast: Cora Ostrander, Walter Pruitt
Plot: Walter Thibault, a bookbinder, is given a diary to rebind and notices the pages have been rearranged to conceal a confession. The sequence, when restored, names Vernon Hargrove, the diarist's closest friend, and the binder is warned to destroy the evidence. A week later, the rearranged diary has cost Walter a friendship and a good night's sleep. Over a long evening, Vernon tells Walter a story about the rearranged diary that nobody else has heard. Walter keeps coming back to the rearranged diary, convinced that the answer is still there. In the drawing room, Walter gathers the suspects and finally explains.

Title: The Gridded Martian Rain
Cast: Marcus Ostrander, Vernon Merrick, Hollis Sutterfield
Plot: Hollis Delacroix, a weather technician on a terraformed Mars, notices that the rain falls in a perfect grid pattern over one particular valley. Wanda Thibault, the valley's lone farmer, has been rationing the rain by hand, and refuses to explain how. Late at night, Hollis finds one last clue about the gridded Martian rain that had been overlooked from the start. Rumours about the gridded Martian rain spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. A new horizon rises on the viewscreen, quiet and green.

Title: The Homing Mare
Cast: Marcus Thibault, Wanda Sutterfield, Marcus Delacroix, Eleanor Ostrander
Plot: Dale Delacroix, a horse trader with a grudge, wins a grey mare in a card game and discovers that the animal can find its way home to any ranch in the county. The mare leads Dale to Hollis Thibault's hidden ranch, where the horse stolen from Dale's own family twenty years ago still waits. Hollis warns that the homing mare will ruin everyone involved, and Dale refuses to listen. A week later, the homing mare has cost Dale a friendship and a good night's sleep. Dale rides out at sunrise without looking back.

Title: The Package with the Thumb
Cast: Lakshmi Ayyadurai, Revathi Subramaniam
Plot: Vasanthi Thirunavukkarasu, a delivery cyclist in a crowded port city, picks up a package at the wrong address and discovers it holds a human thumb. The thumb belongs to Revathi Velusamy, the city's most respected surgeon, and the print on it unlocks a vault of hospital records. Late at night, Vasanthi finds one last clue about the package with the thumb that had been overlooked from the start. Vasanthi keeps coming back to the package with the thumb, convinced that the answer is still there. For one afternoon it seems that the package with the thumb might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. The money is never found, and the city quietly changes hands.

Title: The Weeping Lullaby
Cast: Takeshi Sakuradaira, Daisuke Hakamadajima, Daisuke Ishizumi, Daisuke Aokawa
Plot: Yuki Mizoguro, a laundress at a seaside hotel, hums a lullaby that makes every guest weep, and is promoted to the resident singer. Shinji Tsugawara, the hotel owner, begins selling tickets, and the lullaby loses its power the moment it becomes a show. The more Yuki learns about the weeping lullaby, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Over a long evening, Shinji tells Yuki a story about the weeping lullaby that nobody else has heard. The festival becomes an annual tradition, with everyone in the key of their choice.

Title: The Identical Umbrellas
Cast: Mei Lo, Yee Ngai, Siu Yip
Plot: Siu Lo, a night-bus driver, realises that every passenger on board is carrying an identical black umbrella. Kwok Szeto, the last to board, takes the empty seat beside the driver and explains that tonight's route has been planned for months. Late at night, Siu finds one last clue about the identical umbrellas that had been overlooked from the start. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the identical umbrellas, and Siu starts to suspect Kwok. Siu survives, though the evidence is never recovered.

Title: The Satchel of Love Letters
Cast: Dolores Sutterfield, Hollis Delacroix
Plot: Eleanor Hargrove, a mail rider on the long trail between two frontier towns, finds a satchel of letters addressed to the same woman in a dozen hands. The woman, Lenore Delacroix, died years ago, but the letters keep arriving, and Eleanor follows them to a church whose bell has been silent for a decade. As the season turns, the satchel of love letters becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. The more Eleanor learns about the satchel of love letters, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Eleanor is forced to make an unpopular choice about the satchel of love letters and faces the consequences alone. A last standoff on the main street settles the matter once and for all.

Title: The Faces in the Honeycomb
Cast: Marcus Delacroix, Dale Merrick, Hollis Lindqvist
Plot: Eleanor Pruitt, a village beekeeper, finds that the bees have begun to build their combs in the shape of human faces. One of the faces is Walter Okonkwo, the village priest, who has been missing since the last harvest, and the bees will not stop humming the priest's name. A week later, the faces in the honeycomb has cost Eleanor a friendship and a good night's sleep. As the season turns, the faces in the honeycomb becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Late at night, Eleanor finds one last clue about the faces in the honeycomb that had been overlooked from the start. Only a recording of the final hour remains, and nobody dares to play it.

Title: The Bird-Summoning Flute
Cast: Revathi Sivakumaran, Karthikeyan Chidambaram, Kalyani Annamalai, Revathi Chidambaram
Plot: Kalyani Chidambaram, a pawn shop owner, takes a flute as collateral and finds that every note summons a different bird. Lakshmi Thirunavukkarasu, the borrower, returns with enough cash to claim the flute, but the birds refuse to let the shop owner give it back. Kalyani writes everything about the bird-summoning flute down, in case no one believes it later. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Kalyani thinks about the bird-summoning flute. Kalyani keeps coming back to the bird-summoning flute, convinced that the answer is still there. The curtain falls on thunderous applause and a chorus that will not go home.

Title: The Hundred Envelopes
Cast: Anitha Thampi, Gopan Ammal
Plot: Radhakrishnan Vaidyar, a village postwoman, is asked by a dying neighbour to hand-deliver a hundred identical envelopes to a hundred different addresses. Every envelope holds a single key, and Radhakrishnan slowly works out that Maya Ammal is stitching a map out of the places they open. Radhakrishnan is forced to make an unpopular choice about the hundred envelopes and faces the consequences alone. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the hundred envelopes, and Radhakrishnan starts to suspect Maya. In the end, Radhakrishnan accepts what cannot be repaired and begins again at dawn.

Title: The Mayors' Summit Invitation
Cast: Marcus Okonkwo, Lenore Okonkwo, Marcus Sutterfield, Dale Lindqvist
Plot: Eleanor Sutterfield, a village mayor who has never been outside the county, is invited to a summit of mayors in a city that has never heard of the village. Lenore Delacroix, a clerk, confesses to inventing the invitation as a joke, and Eleanor decides to attend anyway. Eleanor keeps coming back to the mayors' summit invitation, convinced that the answer is still there. Rumours about the mayors' summit invitation spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. The more Eleanor learns about the mayors' summit invitation, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. The whole town squeezes into one room for a deeply awkward reveal.

Title: The Washed-Out Bridge
Cast: Senthil Sivakumaran, Vasanthi Subramaniam, Revathi Chidambaram, Murugesan Chidambaram
Plot: Lakshmi Sivakumaran, a seamstress for a travelling opera troupe, is forced to take the stage when the entire company is stuck at a washed-out bridge.

Title: The Last Crossing
Cast: Narelle Dunmore, Bruce Dunmore, Gary Dunmore
Plot: Bruce Dunmore, a ferry pilot on a lake that is slowly drying up, is ordered to make the last scheduled crossing with a single passenger. The passenger is Jodie Tolhurst, who built the dam that drained the lake, and who asks to be taken to an island that no longer has any water around it. The more Bruce learns about the last crossing, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Bruce writes everything about the last crossing down, in case no one believes it later. The last shot is an ordinary morning, with nothing and everything changed.

Title: Rails Beneath the Snow
Cast: Anatoly Beloselsky, Vera Kuprashova, Mitya Zhelyabov
Plot: In the winter of 1942, a railway repair crew of seven women and one wounded sergeant is stranded at a siding west of Stalingrad with a locomotive that has no coal. Their orders are to keep a single stretch of track open so that a hospital train can pass at dawn, but the line has been bombed in three places and the nearest village was evacuated a week ago. Foreman Zinaida Pavlovna, a former schoolteacher, decides to burn the wooden sleepers from an abandoned branch line to make steam, and the crew works through the night to relay track by hand. Their radio picks up a German patrol only a few kilometres away, and the sergeant, who can barely stand, volunteers to lead them away from the siding. Zinaida refuses to let him go alone and sends the youngest worker, a fifteen-year-old named Lida, to flag down the train if the signal lamp fails. At four in the morning the patrol arrives, and the women fight them off from behind the locomotive using shovels, a flare gun and a stack of frozen rails. The hospital train passes at dawn with its lamps dark and its wounded unaware that they have been saved. Afterwards the crew walks home across the plain in a line, singing quietly, with the sergeant carried on a rail stretcher. The film closes on the siding in the morning light, the track unbroken behind them and nobody left to witness it. A final title card records that the siding was renamed after Zinaida Pavlovna, though she never learned of it and went back to teaching.

Title: The Unbroadcast Script
Cast: Emre Yaşarel, Cem Gökbulut
Plot: Aylin Polatkan, a radio detective-show actor, receives a threatening letter written in the exact words of a script that was never broadcast. Deniz Tunçdemir, the writer, is dead, and the script's last page reveals a murder that has not yet happened. Aylin keeps coming back to the unbroadcast script, convinced that the answer is still there. Rumours about the unbroadcast script spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. The city goes on as it always does, with its lights low and its secrets high.

Title: The Seal-Calling Pipes
Cast: Wanda Pruitt, Dolores Ostrander, Dolores Hargrove
Plot: Wanda Hargrove, a bagpipe maker, discovers that a customer has been secretly using the pipes to call seals out of the sea. Dolores Thibault, the customer, is trying to lure a particular seal that has swallowed a wedding ring. Rumours about the seal-calling pipes spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. Wanda keeps coming back to the seal-calling pipes, convinced that the answer is still there. Wanda delivers the closing number without a trace of nerves.

Title: Monsoon Heist
Cast: Suryakant Ranadive, Pallavi Bhosekar, Hemant Dhawalkar
Plot: During a record Mumbai monsoon, six strangers recruited by a retired magician plan to rob the vault of a diamond merchant while the city is paralysed by floods. The crew includes a deaf locksmith, a street-theatre actress, a failed civil engineer and a pigeon trainer whose birds carry instructions between rooftops. The plan depends on the rain remaining heavy for exactly four hours, so the crew spends the week before the job obsessively watching weather reports. On the night, the magician reveals that the vault has already been emptied by someone else, and that the real purpose of the robbery is to retrieve a ledger hidden in the merchant's safe. The merchant's nephew, who has secretly been feeding them information, turns out to be an inspector from the Economic Offences Wing. The crew must decide whether to hand over the ledger or to burn it in the flooded basement. A rising tide forces the vault door shut with the locksmith still inside, and the actress has to improvise a rescue by pretending to be the merchant's daughter on the telephone. The pigeons guide the engineer to a hidden drain that leads out under the street. By morning the ledger has been delivered to a newspaper and the six thieves have vanished across the flooded city, each carrying nothing but a single wet receipt. A short coda shows the magician on a train to Pune, performing the same coin trick for a child who is not in the least impressed. Rumours place the ledger in three different offices, and the rain over Mumbai refuses to stop for a full week afterwards, as though the city were holding its breath.

Title: The Prospective Confessions
Cast: Marcus Thibault, Vernon Sutterfield, Walter Delacroix, Wanda Lindqvist
Plot: Wanda Okonkwo, a prison chaplain, begins to receive confessions from inmates about crimes that have not been committed yet. The confessions are all being dictated by Walter Thibault, a warden who wants the chaplain to prevent every one of them. A week later, the prospective confessions has cost Wanda a friendship and a good night's sleep. The more Wanda learns about the prospective confessions, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Wanda walks away with nothing but a clean name.

Title: The Forgetting Hour
Cast: Elias Vandermeer, Cora Delacroix, Walt Pruitt
Plot: Detective Sam Garrity wakes up on a bench in a rain-soaked harbour district with a bullet graze on his temple and no memory of who he is or why he carries a stranger's revolver. Piecing together his own life from receipts, a hotel key and a half-burned photograph, he learns that he was hired to find a missing shipping clerk who may have seen a murder. Every witness he questions seems to recognise him, and none will say what he was like. As the trail leads to a nightclub owned by the city's most dangerous man, Garrity begins to suspect that the person he is hunting for is himself.

Title: The Sourdough Starter
Cast: Dale Okonkwo, Vernon Lindqvist
Plot: Dolores Okonkwo, a cattle drive cook who guards a secret sourdough starter, becomes the target of a rival trail boss who wants the recipe. Cora Ostrander, the trail boss, turns out to be a pastry chef from the East who left civilisation behind for exactly this bread. The more Dolores learns about the sourdough starter, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Nobody agrees on what the sourdough starter really means, least of all Cora. Dolores writes everything about the sourdough starter down, in case no one believes it later. Dolores hangs up the gun belt and stays on the porch.

Title: The Burnt Loaf
Cast: Wanda Pruitt, Cora Sutterfield, Marcus Thibault, Walter Hargrove
Plot: Wanda Hargrove, a failed baker, becomes famous overnight when a customer mistakes a burnt loaf for a conceptual art installation. The gallery owner Dolores Delacroix demands twelve more burnt loaves for a retrospective, and Wanda can no longer make them badly on purpose. Rumours about the burnt loaf spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. Late at night, Wanda finds one last clue about the burnt loaf that had been overlooked from the start. The more Wanda learns about the burnt loaf, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Wanda resolves to tell the truth from now on, for roughly a week.

Title: The Freed Lamp Spirit
Cast: Selin Özdilek, Burak Karabulut, Deniz Aksoylu
Plot: Zeynep Tunçdemir, a lamplighter in a city where the streetlamps hold trapped spirits, accidentally releases one on a cold winter night. The spirit demands to be taken home, and Selin Karabulut, the city's alderman, wants all the spirits returned to their lamps by dawn. Zeynep writes everything about the freed lamp spirit down, in case no one believes it later. Zeynep keeps coming back to the freed lamp spirit, convinced that the answer is still there. Zeynep is forced to make an unpopular choice about the freed lamp spirit and faces the consequences alone. Zeynep takes up the burden gladly and sets out at first light.

Title: The Spiral Trench
Cast: Duncan Sutherby, Duncan Thibodault, Mireille Sutherby
Plot: Gilles Thibodault, an ocean-floor cartographer, discovers that the trench being charted has been steadily deepening in the shape of a spiral. Lorne Wharnecliffe, the submarine pilot, descends to the bottom and radios back that the spiral is an enormous, carefully made staircase. As the season turns, the spiral trench becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Lorne warns that the spiral trench will ruin everyone involved, and Gilles refuses to listen. Over a long evening, Lorne tells Gilles a story about the spiral trench that nobody else has heard. The survivors set a new course toward a star nobody has named.

Title: The Dough Creatures
Cast: Eleanor Thibault, Lenore Thibault, Dale Delacroix, Dolores Pruitt
Plot: Marcus Sutterfield, a village baker, finds that the bread dough rises into small animals that run away at dawn. Hollis Sutterfield, a travelling witch, offers to buy the secret recipe, but the animals refuse to return to the oven. A week later, the dough creatures has cost Marcus a friendship and a good night's sleep. Rumours about the dough creatures spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. Nobody agrees on what the dough creatures really means, least of all Hollis. Marcus takes up the burden gladly and sets out at first light.

Title: The Note Reading Tomorrow
Cast: Jodie Yarrowood, Jodie Costain, Kerry Mulgrave
Plot: Jodie Hargadon, a ferry stewardess, finds a passenger dead in a locked cabin with a half-eaten orange and a note reading only the word tomorrow. Kerry Pemberthy, the ship's purser, has been selling tomorrow's tickets for decades, and the dead passenger discovered the fraud. Jodie writes everything about the note reading tomorrow down, in case no one believes it later. Nobody agrees on what the note reading tomorrow really means, least of all Kerry. Someone begins quietly removing every trace of the note reading tomorrow, and Jodie starts to suspect Kerry. The culprit is led away, and the guests depart in uneasy silence.

Title: The Labelled Suitcase
Cast: Walter Ostrander, Wanda Hargrove
Plot: Marcus Delacroix, a young clerk in a lost-property office, finds a suitcase labelled with the clerk's own name, left there fifteen years earlier. Inside is a set of instructions from Walter Lindqvist, an eccentric aunt, for a series of increasingly ridiculous errands. Marcus keeps coming back to the labelled suitcase, convinced that the answer is still there. The more Marcus learns about the labelled suitcase, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Walter warns that the labelled suitcase will ruin everyone involved, and Marcus refuses to listen. Marcus resolves to tell the truth from now on, for roughly a week.

Title: The Shared Autumn Ladder
Cast: Narelle Tolhurst, Jodie Costain, Clive Tolhurst
Plot: Kerry Ironbridge, a seasonal fruit picker, shares a ladder each autumn with a stranger who never gives a name. On the last day of harvest, Clive Pemberthy, the stranger, writes a name on the last apple and hands it over without a word. Clive warns that the shared autumn ladder will ruin everyone involved, and Kerry refuses to listen. The more Kerry learns about the shared autumn ladder, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Nobody agrees on what the shared autumn ladder really means, least of all Clive. The two begin again in a small house by the sea.

Title: The Suitcase in the Lock
Cast: Boris Orlov, Natalya Orlov, Natalya Kuznetsov, Dmitri Orlov
Plot: Dmitri Dobrolyubov, a river lock keeper, finds a locked suitcase caught in the gates and a trail of wet footprints leading in the wrong direction. The suitcase belongs to Irina Verbitsky, who is both the drowned man and the murderer, depending on which lock is considered first. Over a long evening, Irina tells Dmitri a story about the suitcase in the lock that nobody else has heard. Dmitri is forced to make an unpopular choice about the suitcase in the lock and faces the consequences alone. Dmitri returns to the quiet village with one question still unanswered.

Title: The Sold Island
Cast: Lenore Ostrander, Wanda Ostrander
Plot: Lenore Pruitt, a lighthouse supply boat captain, learns that the island being served has been sold and that the keeper has not been told. Vernon Okonkwo, the keeper, already knows, and has been hiding the notices in the lamp room for a year so that Lenore will keep visiting. A week later, the sold island has cost Lenore a friendship and a good night's sleep. Lenore keeps coming back to the sold island, convinced that the answer is still there. The community gathers, and a quiet reconciliation settles over the final scene.

Title: The Prodigy's Borrowed Voice
Cast: Radhakrishnan Ammal, Gopan Thampi
Plot: Thankamma Vaidyar, a boy soprano in a provincial church, is overlooked in favour of a visiting prodigy who cannot actually sing. Sreedevi Panicker, the prodigy's manager, has been mouthing to a hidden recording, and begs Thankamma to provide the voice from behind the organ. For one afternoon it seems that the prodigy's borrowed voice might be forgotten, but the town has other plans. As the season turns, the prodigy's borrowed voice becomes the only subject anyone is willing to discuss. Thankamma takes a final bow under the old marquee.

Title: The Window Display Crime
Cast: Vernon Ostrander, Vernon Delacroix, Lenore Ostrander, Marcus Merrick
Plot: Eleanor Pruitt, a window dresser at a department store, stages a mannequin scene that mirrors a crime the police have not discovered. Vernon Sutterfield, a detective, stops outside the window each day, and eventually asks to see the mannequin's pockets. An unexpected act of kindness from a stranger changes how Eleanor thinks about the window display crime. Rumours about the window display crime spread faster than the truth, and soon even strangers have an opinion. The more Eleanor learns about the window display crime, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. The city goes on as it always does, with its lights low and its secrets high.

Title: The Growing House
Cast: Meenal Bhosekar, Devendra Dhawalkar, Kabir Vaidya
Plot: Aravind Moitra, a family dog walker in a quiet suburb, begins to notice that a particular house has more windows each day. Sunita Sengupta, a neighbour who counts the windows, has vanished into the house, and the dogs refuse to walk past it. Aravind is forced to make an unpopular choice about the growing house and faces the consequences alone. Sunita warns that the growing house will ruin everyone involved, and Aravind refuses to listen. Aravind locks the door and waits for the final knock.

Title: The Backward Shadows
Cast: Hollis Pruitt, Lenore Hargrove, Lenore Delacroix, Cora Lindqvist
Plot: Wanda Sutterfield, a young night watchman in a walled city, notices that the shadows at the gate move in the opposite direction from their owners. Lenore Pruitt, the gate captain, has traded away a shadow for safe passage and wants it back before the festival. Wanda writes everything about the backward shadows down, in case no one believes it later. Wanda keeps coming back to the backward shadows, convinced that the answer is still there. The final spell is spoken in a whisper, and the world quietly shifts.

Title: Operation Teacup
Cast: Algernon Pettigrew, Dulcie Warrender, Basil Haythornthwaite
Plot: In 1944 the War Office hatches a plan to fool the German high command into believing that the Allied invasion will land at Brighton, by staging an enormous fake tea party on the beach. The mission falls to Major Hubert Pennywhistle, a nervous quartermaster with a talent for catering and no talent for secrecy. He recruits a troupe of retired music-hall performers, a vicar with a model railway, and a brass band that can only play one tune. The fake pier, built from painted canvas, collapses in the first gale, and the cardboard tanks are eaten by seagulls. A German spy disguised as a deckchair attendant reports back that the tea party is the most heavily defended event in England, which delights the War Office. Hubert learns that his fake invasion has become so convincing that the German commander is diverting two divisions to meet it. He is ordered to keep the party going for another week, and the entire village contributes its entire sugar ration to make the cakes look real. On the final day a real German reconnaissance plane circles low over the beach, and the performers must pretend to be the Royal Navy by singing every sea shanty they know. The plane flies away satisfied. On the real invasion morning, Hubert is quietly informed that the beach tea party is the secret reason the real landing succeeded, and he is awarded a medal that he promptly mistakes for a biscuit tin lid. The beach is still there, the film reminds us, and so is the tea. Years later the War Office quietly commissions a second fake tea party at a different beach, and nobody can find the vicar or the model railway.

Title: The Abandoned Swing
Cast: Rohit Ranadive, Aravind Pandharkar, Devendra Sengupta
Plot: Vikrant, a playground swing, sets out to find the child who stopped coming to the park. Meenal, a kindly crow, carries the swing's message to a window, and the child, now grown, comes back with a child of their own. The more Vikrant learns about the abandoned swing, the less certain it becomes who should be trusted. Late at night, Vikrant finds one last clue about the abandoned swing that had been overlooked from the start. Vikrant writes everything about the abandoned swing down, in case no one believes it later. Vikrant finally reaches the end of the journey and giggles.

Title: The Sunrise Keeper's Bell
Cast: Wanda Lindqvist, Walter Sutterfield, Hollis Merrick
Plot: Walter, a young badger who hates mornings, is appointed the keeper of the sunrise for a single day. Marcus, the sleepy sun, is reluctant to rise and requires a special song only the badger knows. Walter writes everything about the sunrise keeper's bell down, in case no one believes it later. Nobody agrees on what the sunrise keeper's bell really means, least of all Marcus. Marcus warns that the sunrise keeper's bell will ruin everyone involved, and Walter refuses to listen. Walter waves goodbye to the credits and tiptoes home.
